industry.name: Nuclear Energy & Reactor Safety
industry.description: Reactor safety and operations, radiation protection and health physics, regulatory licensing and compliance, safety analysis and risk (PRA), and emergency preparedness and security. 80 roles across 5 clusters.

roles.title: Non-Licensed Operator
roles.degree_detail: A high school diploma or equivalent is the baseline, and many non-licensed operators enter directly from the U.S. Navy nuclear propulsion program or a trade background. Employers provide a multi-week Generic Fundamentals and plant-specific initial training program accredited through INPO, followed by on-the-job qualification cards. Associate degrees in nuclear or power plant technology are common and can shorten time to the licensed operator pipeline.
roles.experience: 0-2 years

skills.name: Plant System Walkdowns
skills.description: You walk down assigned systems in the turbine building and auxiliary areas, logging pump, valve, and tank parameters so the control room keeps an accurate picture of plant status. You learn to recognize abnormal noise, vibration, and leakage before they become reportable conditions.

skills.name: Equipment Operation and Alignment
skills.description: You start, stop, and align pumps, compressors, and valves in the field under direction of the control room. You verify component lineups against approved procedures so safety-related trains stay operable.

skills.name: Radiation Protection Practices
skills.description: You follow ALARA principles and radiation work permits when entering the radiologically controlled area. You use dosimetry and contamination survey basics to keep your exposure as low as reasonably achievable.

skills.name: Procedure Use and Adherence
skills.description: You perform field tasks step by step using plant procedures, placekeeping each action and stopping when conditions do not match expectations. This place-keeping discipline is foundational to nuclear safety culture.

skills.name: Industrial and Electrical Safety
skills.description: You apply lockout/tagout, confined space, and electrical safety practices around high-energy plant equipment. You protect yourself and tagged-out equipment so maintenance can be performed safely.

skills.name: Logkeeping and Communication
skills.description: You maintain accurate operator logs and use three-way communication when reporting field conditions to the control room. Clear, repeat-back communication prevents errors during evolutions.

roles.description: You are the eyes and hands of the control room in the field, operating and monitoring plant equipment outside the main control area. You perform rounds, support surveillances, and manipulate components during normal and abnormal evolutions, forming the first line of defense in keeping the reactor and its support systems operating safely. This role is the common entry point into the operations career path toward an NRC license.

roles.title: Reactor Operator Trainee
roles.degree_detail: Trainees typically hold a high school diploma plus significant plant experience, an associate degree in a nuclear or technical field, or a Navy nuclear background. The utility runs an INPO-accredited initial license training program built to ANSI/ANS-3.1 personnel qualification standards. Successful trainees sit for the NRC Reactor Operator written exam and operating test to earn their license.
roles.experience: 0-2 years

skills.name: Reactor Theory Fundamentals
skills.description: You study neutron multiplication, reactivity coefficients, and decay heat so you understand why the core behaves as it does. This foundation lets you anticipate reactor response during startup, power changes, and shutdown.

skills.name: Control Room Panel Familiarization
skills.description: You learn the layout and function of control boards, indications, and annunciators under the supervision of licensed operators. You build the pattern recognition needed to scan panels and detect off-normal conditions quickly.

skills.name: Simulator Evolutions
skills.description: You practice plant startups, shutdowns, and transients on the full-scope control room simulator. Repeated simulator time builds the muscle memory and crew communication you will need once licensed.

skills.name: Emergency and Abnormal Procedures
skills.description: You study emergency operating procedures and abnormal operating procedures that govern response to trips, losses of coolant, and other events. You learn the symptom-based logic that keeps the core cooled under accident conditions.

skills.name: Systems Knowledge
skills.description: You master the design, flow paths, and interlocks of major plant systems such as reactor coolant, feedwater, and emergency core cooling. Deep systems knowledge is tested directly on the NRC license exam.

skills.name: Conduct of Operations Standards
skills.description: You internalize formality of operations, self-checking, and peer-checking expectations that govern every licensed action. These behaviors are graded continuously throughout license training.

roles.description: You are in the formal pipeline toward an NRC Reactor Operator license, spending roughly a year to eighteen months in classroom, systems, and simulator training. You learn to manipulate reactor controls and respond to transients while being evaluated against ANSI/ANS training standards. Completing this program and passing the NRC exam qualifies you to operate the reactor, a safety-critical role at the heart of the plant.

roles.title: Auxiliary Equipment Operator
roles.degree_detail: A high school diploma or equivalent is required, with mechanical aptitude demonstrated through prior industrial, military, or trades experience. You complete plant-specific non-licensed operator training accredited by INPO and progress through equipment qualification cards. Many auxiliary operators use this role as a stepping stone into the NRC-licensed operator pipeline.
roles.experience: 1-3 years

skills.name: Rotating Equipment Monitoring
skills.description: You monitor pumps, fans, diesel generators, and other rotating equipment, trending bearing temperatures, vibration, and lube oil condition. Early detection of degradation keeps safety-related trains available.

skills.name: Valve Manipulation and Lineups
skills.description: You operate manual and motor-operated valves to establish system lineups for surveillances and evolutions. You independently verify positions so no mispositioned component defeats a safety function.

skills.name: Tagout Execution
skills.description: You hang and clear equipment clearance orders to isolate components for maintenance. Correct boundary verification protects both workers and plant safety systems.

skills.name: Chemistry and Fluid Sampling
skills.description: You draw samples and read local instrumentation for plant chemistry and fluid systems. Accurate field data supports control room decisions on water quality and system health.

skills.name: Fire Watch and Transient Combustible Control
skills.description: You stand fire watches and control transient combustibles in safety-significant areas. These actions protect fire-safe-shutdown capability required by plant licensing.

skills.name: Severe Weather and Flooding Response
skills.description: You execute field actions for storms, high winds, and external flooding per abnormal procedures. Timely staging of equipment preserves the plant's defense against natural hazards.

roles.description: You operate and tend balance-of-plant and support equipment across the site, extending the control room's reach into the field. You stage equipment for evolutions, respond to field alarms, and support maintenance isolations, keeping the systems that back up reactor safety reliable and available. The role builds the systems knowledge that feeds directly into reactor operator training.

roles.title: Research Reactor Operator
roles.degree_detail: Research reactor operators are often undergraduate students, graduate students, or staff in nuclear engineering or a physical science, though a four-year degree is not universally required by the NRC. You train against facility-specific procedures and the ANSI/ANS-15.4 standard for research reactor operator selection and training. You must pass an NRC Reactor Operator license exam specific to that facility before manipulating the controls unsupervised.
roles.experience: 0-3 years

skills.name: Low-Power Reactor Operation
skills.description: You start up, operate, and shut down a university or test reactor at low thermal power for experiments and training. You manage reactivity using control rods while keeping the core within license limits.

skills.name: Experiment Support
skills.description: You configure the reactor and irradiation facilities for neutron activation analysis, isotope production, and student labs. You verify that each experiment stays within reactivity and safety-analysis bounds.

skills.name: Instrumentation Interpretation
skills.description: You read nuclear instrumentation channels, period meters, and radiation monitors to confirm expected core behavior. You recognize when indications call for a manual scram.

skills.name: Technical Specification Compliance
skills.description: You operate within the facility technical specifications and the reactor safety analysis report. You log limiting conditions for operation and surveillance results precisely.

skills.name: Radiation Survey and Sample Handling
skills.description: You survey irradiated samples and manage radioactive material under the facility radiation protection program. You keep dose to students, staff, and the public well within limits.

skills.name: Tours and Public Safety Communication
skills.description: You explain reactor operation and safety systems to visitors, students, and regulators. Clear communication supports the facility's education and outreach mission.

roles.description: You operate a university, research, or test reactor that supports education, isotope production, and materials research rather than power generation. You manipulate controls, support experiments, and keep the facility within its license and technical specifications, ensuring safety for students, staff, and the public. These facilities are a key training ground for the broader Texas nuclear workforce.

roles.title: Nuclear Instrumentation and Controls Technician
roles.degree_detail: An associate degree in instrumentation, electronics, or electrical technology is the common entry credential, and Navy electronics or fire control backgrounds transfer well. You complete an INPO-accredited I&C maintenance training program and qualify on plant-specific equipment through task performance evaluations. Continued qualification is maintained through periodic requalification and procedure training.
roles.experience: 0-3 years

skills.name: Instrument Calibration
skills.description: You calibrate pressure, level, flow, and temperature transmitters that feed reactor protection and control systems. Accurate calibration keeps safety-related setpoints trustworthy.

skills.name: Nuclear Instrumentation Channels
skills.description: You test and maintain source range, intermediate range, and power range nuclear instrumentation. These channels provide the reactor trip signals that protect the core.

skills.name: Loop Checks and Troubleshooting
skills.description: You perform signal loop checks and isolate faults across sensors, cabling, and controllers. Methodical troubleshooting restores channel operability without introducing errors.

skills.name: Surveillance Testing
skills.description: You execute technical specification surveillances on protection and actuation logic. You document as-found and as-left data that proves safety functions remain operable.

skills.name: Digital Control System Support
skills.description: You support digital control and protection platforms used in modern and advanced plants. You follow configuration controls so software-based safety functions stay verified.

skills.name: Work Order and Procedure Compliance
skills.description: You perform maintenance under approved work orders, clearances, and foreign material exclusion controls. Discipline here prevents inadvertent actuations and plant transients.

roles.description: You keep the sensors, logic, and actuation equipment of the reactor protection and control systems accurate and operable. You calibrate instruments, run surveillance tests, and troubleshoot faults so the signals that trip the reactor and actuate safety systems can be trusted. Your work is a direct contributor to the plant's defense-in-depth safety case.

roles.title: SMR Operations Technician Trainee
roles.degree_detail: An associate degree in a nuclear, mechanical, electrical, or process technology field is typical, with military nuclear experience valued. Vendors and operators run design-specific training programs aligned to INPO accreditation and ANSI/ANS training standards, often tied to the plant's NRC operator licensing basis. Because many SMR control rooms oversee multiple modules, the NRC evaluates design-specific license scopes before you can operate independently.
roles.experience: 0-2 years

skills.name: Passive Safety System Fundamentals
skills.description: You learn how small modular reactor passive cooling and natural circulation features remove decay heat without active pumps. Understanding these features is central to how advanced designs stay safe.

skills.name: Multi-Module Monitoring
skills.description: You train to monitor several reactor modules from a shared control room using integrated digital displays. You practice maintaining situational awareness across modules at once.

skills.name: Digital Human-System Interface
skills.description: You operate the digital human-system interface and alarm management features of an advanced control room. You learn to trust and verify automated indications rather than defer to them blindly.

skills.name: Factory and Modular Equipment Knowledge
skills.description: You study the factory-fabricated, modular design of SMR systems and how components are assembled on site. This knowledge supports commissioning and operations of first-of-a-kind units.

skills.name: Procedure and Simulator Practice
skills.description: You rehearse startups, load changes, and transients on design-specific simulators. Early simulator exposure builds the habits needed for eventual NRC licensing.

skills.name: Conduct of Operations Basics
skills.description: You adopt self-checking, peer-checking, and formal communications from the first day of training. These behaviors carry directly into a licensed operator role on an advanced plant.

roles.description: You are training to operate a small modular or advanced reactor, a growing opportunity as Texas pursues new nuclear deployment. You learn passive safety concepts, digital control rooms, and multi-module monitoring that distinguish these designs from the large light-water fleet. You are building toward a licensed operations role on first-of-a-kind units that will shape the next generation of safe reactor operation.

roles.title: Licensed Reactor Operator
roles.degree_detail: Most licensed reactor operators advance from non-licensed operator roles after completing an INPO-accredited initial license training program built to ANSI/ANS-3.1. An associate degree or equivalent military nuclear experience is typical, and some hold four-year degrees. You earned the role by passing the NRC Reactor Operator written exam and operating test, and you maintain it through a continuing requalification program.
roles.experience: 3-6 years

skills.name: Reactor Control Manipulation
skills.description: You manipulate control rods, boron concentration, and plant controls to raise, lower, and hold reactor power safely. You keep the core within thermal and reactivity limits throughout every evolution.

skills.name: Transient and Casualty Response
skills.description: You diagnose and respond to reactor trips, losses of coolant, and other transients using emergency operating procedures. Your rapid, procedure-based actions keep the core cooled and contained.

skills.name: Panel Monitoring and Diagnosis
skills.description: You continuously scan control boards and annunciators, diagnosing off-normal conditions from subtle indication changes. Early diagnosis prevents small upsets from escalating.

skills.name: Reactivity Management
skills.description: You plan and execute reactivity changes conservatively, accounting for xenon, temperature, and rod worth. Disciplined reactivity management is a graded fundamental of safe operation.

skills.name: Formal Crew Communication
skills.description: You use three-way communication, repeat-backs, and standardized phraseology with the crew during evolutions. This formality eliminates ambiguity when actions are time-critical.

skills.name: Technical Specification Awareness
skills.description: You track limiting conditions for operation and required actions in real time. You ensure the plant never operates outside its licensing basis on your watch.

roles.description: You hold an NRC Reactor Operator license and manipulate the controls of a commercial reactor from the main control room. You execute startups, shutdowns, power changes, and emergency response under the direction of senior licensed personnel, serving as a primary safeguard of the core and the public. Your licensed judgment is a cornerstone of the plant's layered safety defenses.

roles.title: Control Room Supervisor
roles.degree_detail: You advance from a licensed Reactor Operator role, or enter directly on an SRO instant path with a four-year engineering degree and plant experience. Qualification requires completing INPO-accredited senior license training aligned to ANSI/ANS-3.1 and passing the NRC Senior Reactor Operator exam. You maintain the license through ongoing requalification, simulator evaluations, and medical qualification.
roles.experience: 6-10 years

skills.name: Crew Command and Control
skills.description: You direct the licensed operators at the controls, setting the pace and maintaining command of plant evolutions. You keep the crew aligned so actions stay deliberate and conservative.

skills.name: Procedure Oversight
skills.description: You oversee entry into and transitions between normal, abnormal, and emergency operating procedures. You confirm the crew is in the correct procedure for current plant conditions.

skills.name: Reactivity Review and Approval
skills.description: You review and approve reactivity manipulation plans before the crew executes them. Your independent check guards against reactivity management errors.

skills.name: Conservative Decision Making
skills.description: You apply conservative decision-making and the questioning attitude when plant conditions are uncertain. You stop evolutions when safety margins are in doubt.

skills.name: Technical Specification Compliance
skills.description: You interpret technical specifications and direct required actions within allowed completion times. You prevent inadvertent entry into prohibited operating conditions.

skills.name: Evolution Briefings
skills.description: You conduct pre-job briefings that establish contingencies, critical steps, and error-likely situations. Strong briefings set the crew up to catch and recover from mistakes.

roles.description: You hold an NRC Senior Reactor Operator license and supervise the licensed operators manipulating reactor controls. You direct evolutions, approve reactivity plans, and ensure the crew stays within the licensing basis, acting as a key safety authority inside the control room. Your oversight converts individual operator actions into disciplined, defense-in-depth crew performance.

roles.title: Shift Technical Advisor
roles.degree_detail: A four-year degree in engineering or a physical science is the standard requirement, reflecting the position's origin in NRC post-TMI action plan requirements. You complete plant-specific shift technical advisor training covering thermal-hydraulics, accident analysis, and emergency procedures. Many advisors also hold or pursue an NRC Senior Reactor Operator license, though the STA function itself emphasizes independent technical assessment.
roles.experience: 4-8 years

skills.name: Accident Diagnosis
skills.description: You provide independent engineering assessment of plant conditions during transients and accidents. Your diagnosis gives the shift manager an added perspective on core safety status.

skills.name: Thermal-Hydraulic Analysis
skills.description: You evaluate core heat removal, natural circulation, and reactor coolant system behavior under abnormal conditions. This analysis informs decisions that keep the core covered and cooled.

skills.name: Safety Function Monitoring
skills.description: You track the critical safety functions such as subcriticality, core cooling, and containment integrity. You alert the crew when any safety function is challenged or degrading.

skills.name: Emergency Procedure Technical Basis
skills.description: You understand the technical and analytical basis behind emergency operating procedures. You advise the crew when conditions approach the edges of procedural assumptions.

skills.name: Independent Oversight
skills.description: You maintain a step-back, non-manipulative vantage point while the crew operates controls. This independence is the reason the position exists under NRC requirements.

skills.name: Event Communication
skills.description: You translate complex plant behavior into clear briefings for the shift manager and emergency response organization. Clear technical communication accelerates sound decisions.

roles.description: You serve as the degreed engineering advisor on shift, a position created after Three Mile Island to provide independent technical oversight of core safety. You monitor critical safety functions and advise the shift manager during transients and accidents, free from the duty of manipulating controls. Your independent engineering judgment is a deliberate layer in the plant's defense in depth.

roles.title: I&C Safety Systems Engineer
roles.degree_detail: A four-year degree in electrical, nuclear, computer, or systems engineering is required, and an Engineer in Training certificate is a plus. You develop expertise through plant systems training, the station's engineering support personnel program, and mentoring under senior design engineers. Many pursue a Professional Engineer license, which supports credibility in design and licensing work.
roles.experience: 3-7 years

skills.name: Reactor Protection System Engineering
skills.description: You own the design basis and setpoints of the reactor protection and engineered safety features actuation systems. You ensure trip and actuation logic performs within its safety analysis assumptions.

skills.name: Setpoint and Uncertainty Analysis
skills.description: You calculate instrument setpoints with loop uncertainty methodologies so trips occur before safety limits are reached. Your margins protect the fuel and the reactor coolant boundary.

skills.name: Digital I&C and Cybersecurity
skills.description: You evaluate digital instrumentation platforms for common-cause failure vulnerability and compliance with NRC cyber security requirements. You keep software-based safety functions defensible.

skills.name: Surveillance and Operability Evaluation
skills.description: You assess surveillance results and degraded conditions to judge the operability of safety instrumentation. Your operability determinations keep the plant inside its licensing basis.

skills.name: Modification and Design Review
skills.description: You review and support plant modifications affecting protection and control systems under 10 CFR 50.59. You confirm changes do not create unreviewed safety questions.

skills.name: Root Cause and Trend Analysis
skills.description: You investigate instrumentation failures and trend channel performance across the fleet. Your analysis drives corrective actions that prevent repeat safety system degradation.

roles.description: You are the engineering owner of the instrumentation and control systems that detect unsafe conditions and automatically trip the reactor or actuate safety systems. You maintain setpoints, evaluate operability, and support modifications so these systems perform exactly as the safety analysis assumes. Your work underpins the automatic protection layer of the plant's defense in depth.

roles.title: Operations Training Instructor
roles.degree_detail: Most operations instructors hold a four-year degree and a current or previous NRC Senior Reactor Operator license, which is effectively required to instruct licensed operators. You complete instructor certification under the Systematic Approach to Training and the station's INPO-accredited training program. Continuing qualification keeps your SRO knowledge and instructional skills current.
roles.experience: 5-9 years

skills.name: Simulator Instruction
skills.description: You run full-scope simulator scenarios that drill crews on startups, transients, and accident response. You design scenarios that expose and correct crew performance gaps.

skills.name: Systematic Approach to Training
skills.description: You develop and deliver training using the Systematic Approach to Training required for INPO accreditation. You tie every lesson to analyzed job and task requirements.

skills.name: Crew Performance Evaluation
skills.description: You evaluate operator and crew performance against standards for communications, procedure use, and decision-making. Your assessments feed requalification and license maintenance decisions.

skills.name: Exam Development
skills.description: You write and validate written and operating examinations consistent with NRC and ANSI/ANS standards. Defensible exams ensure only qualified operators stay licensed.

skills.name: Operating Experience Integration
skills.description: You incorporate industry operating experience and plant events into training content. This keeps crews rehearsed on the failure modes that have actually challenged reactors.

skills.name: Fundamentals Instruction
skills.description: You teach reactor theory, thermodynamics, and plant systems to initial license classes. Strong fundamentals instruction builds operators who understand why procedures work.

roles.description: You train and evaluate the operators who run the reactor, delivering initial license, requalification, and continuing training. You lead simulator evolutions, build exams, and assess crew performance so every licensed operator meets exacting safety standards. By maintaining the competence of the operating crews, you reinforce the human layer of nuclear safety.

roles.title: Senior Reactor Operator
roles.degree_detail: You advance from a licensed Reactor Operator position or enter on an instant SRO path with a four-year degree and extensive experience. Qualification requires an INPO-accredited senior license program aligned to ANSI/ANS-3.1 and passing the NRC Senior Reactor Operator examination. You sustain the license through continuing requalification, annual simulator evaluations, and medical qualification.
roles.experience: 8+ years

skills.name: Evolution Direction
skills.description: You direct and authorize major plant evolutions including startups, shutdowns, and mode changes. Your authorization is the control point that keeps high-risk evolutions deliberate and safe.

skills.name: Reactivity Manipulation Authority
skills.description: You approve and supervise all reactivity manipulations performed by the reactor operators. Your oversight is a formal barrier against reactivity accidents.

skills.name: Technical Specification Judgment
skills.description: You make real-time operability and technical specification compliance decisions under time pressure. Your interpretations keep the plant within its license during degraded conditions.

skills.name: Emergency Command
skills.description: You command crew response to accidents using emergency operating procedures and emergency plan classifications. You decide protective actions that safeguard the core and the public.

skills.name: Risk-Informed Decision Making
skills.description: You weigh plant risk using configuration risk management and conservative decision principles. You hold the line when production pressure conflicts with safety margin.

skills.name: Crew Oversight and Coaching
skills.description: You set and enforce standards for formality, self-checking, and questioning attitude across the crew. Your example shapes the station's operational safety culture.

roles.description: You hold an NRC Senior Reactor Operator license and carry the authority to direct and authorize operation of the reactor. You supervise evolutions, approve reactivity changes, and make the conservative calls that protect the core, standing as a central safety authority in the control room. Your licensed command is one of the most consequential safety roles at the plant.

roles.title: Shift Manager
roles.degree_detail: Shift managers typically hold a four-year degree and years of experience as a licensed SRO, often progressing through control room supervisor and unit supervisor roles. You maintain an active NRC Senior Reactor Operator license through continuing requalification and simulator evaluations. Leadership and emergency director training complement the technical license requirements.
roles.experience: 10+ years

skills.name: Command of the Shift
skills.description: You hold overall command of the operating shift and the plant during your watch. Every safety-significant decision on shift flows through your authority.

skills.name: Emergency Director Duties
skills.description: You serve as the initial emergency director, classifying events and directing protective actions until relieved. Your prompt classification drives offsite notifications that protect the public.

skills.name: Operational Risk Management
skills.description: You manage plant configuration risk, equipment out-of-service windows, and online maintenance safety. You prevent risk-significant combinations of unavailable equipment.

skills.name: Regulatory Reportability Judgment
skills.description: You determine reportability of events to the NRC and oversee immediate notifications. Accurate, timely reporting maintains the plant's regulatory standing and safety transparency.

skills.name: Crew Leadership
skills.description: You lead a multidisciplinary shift crew, setting expectations for safety culture and conservative operation. Your leadership keeps the crew aligned under normal and emergency conditions.

skills.name: Conservative Decision Authority
skills.description: You exercise final conservative decision-making authority, including shutting down the plant when safety requires. You protect the core even when doing so carries large economic cost.

roles.description: You are the senior licensed authority in charge of the plant on your shift, with command over operations and the initial emergency response. You direct the crew, manage operational risk, and make the final conservative calls that keep the reactor safe, including ordering a shutdown when warranted. Few roles carry more direct responsibility for public safety on a day-to-day basis.

roles.title: Operations Safety Manager
roles.degree_detail: A four-year degree in engineering or a related field plus extensive licensed operations experience is standard, and a current or former NRC Senior Reactor Operator license is strongly preferred. You build credibility through years in control room supervision and operations leadership roles. Advanced training in human performance, root cause analysis, and leadership supports the position.
roles.experience: 12+ years

skills.name: Conduct of Operations Oversight
skills.description: You own the standards and procedures that govern how operations conducts work across all shifts. You drive consistency in formality, procedure use, and human performance stationwide.

skills.name: Human Performance Improvement
skills.description: You analyze operator error trends and deploy human performance tools to reduce events. Your programs attack the error precursors that lead to safety-significant mistakes.

skills.name: Corrective Action Program Leadership
skills.description: You ensure operations findings are captured, screened, and resolved in the corrective action program. You prevent recurrence of conditions that challenge reactor safety.

skills.name: Operational Safety Culture
skills.description: You monitor and strengthen a healthy nuclear safety culture, including a safety-conscious work environment. You ensure staff feel free to raise safety concerns without fear.

skills.name: Regulatory and INPO Interface
skills.description: You engage NRC inspectors and INPO evaluators on operations performance and findings. You translate external oversight into sustained improvement.

skills.name: Operational Risk Governance
skills.description: You govern configuration risk management and online risk policies for the operations organization. Your oversight keeps aggregate plant risk within acceptable limits.

roles.description: You lead the programs and standards that keep the operations organization performing safely across every shift. You drive conduct of operations, human performance, and corrective action so that operator behavior and crew practices stay disciplined and conservative. You are a principal steward of operational safety culture and a key interface with regulators and industry oversight.

roles.title: Operations Training Superintendent
roles.degree_detail: A four-year degree and a current or former NRC Senior Reactor Operator license are expected, along with years of experience as an operations instructor and supervisor. You lead programs accredited by the National Nuclear Accrediting Board through INPO, applying the Systematic Approach to Training. Leadership and training management experience round out the qualifications for this superintendent role.
roles.experience: 10+ years

skills.name: Training Program Accreditation
skills.description: You lead the operations training programs through INPO accreditation and reaccreditation cycles. You ensure the Systematic Approach to Training is applied and documented across all courses.

skills.name: License Training Oversight
skills.description: You oversee initial license and requalification programs that produce and sustain NRC-licensed operators. Your governance keeps license classes meeting NRC and ANSI/ANS standards.

skills.name: Instructor Development
skills.description: You develop and qualify the instructor staff, including maintaining their SRO certifications. A strong instructor bench is essential to producing competent operators.

skills.name: Simulator Fidelity Management
skills.description: You ensure the training simulator remains an accurate, up-to-date model of the plant. High simulator fidelity is required for valid training and NRC exams.

skills.name: Training Effectiveness Evaluation
skills.description: You evaluate whether training actually improves field and control room performance. You close the loop between plant events and training content.

skills.name: Budget and Resource Planning
skills.description: You plan staffing, schedules, and budgets to sustain the operations training pipeline. You balance production demands against the time crews need in the classroom and simulator.

roles.description: You direct the entire operations training organization that qualifies and requalifies the plant's licensed operators. You own program accreditation, instructor quality, and simulator fidelity so that training reliably produces operators who can keep the reactor safe. By safeguarding operator competence, you uphold the human foundation of nuclear safety.

roles.title: Superintendent of Operations
roles.degree_detail: A four-year engineering degree is standard and a graduate degree or management credential is common at this level, paired with a current or former NRC Senior Reactor Operator license. You advance through control room supervisor, shift manager, and operations management roles over many years. Executive and nuclear leadership development programs prepare you for this accountable position.
roles.experience: 15+ years

skills.name: Operations Organization Leadership
skills.description: You lead all operating shifts and the operations support staff for the station. You set direction and standards that every crew carries into the control room.

skills.name: Fleet Safety Standards
skills.description: You implement and enforce fleet and industry operational safety standards across the department. You align station practices with the highest-performing plants.

skills.name: Senior Regulatory Interface
skills.description: You represent operations in senior engagements with the NRC and INPO. You own the operations commitments and performance that regulators scrutinize.

skills.name: Operational Risk Accountability
skills.description: You hold accountability for aggregate operational risk and major evolution readiness, including outages. Your governance ensures the plant never trades safety margin for schedule.

skills.name: Succession and Licensing Pipeline
skills.description: You manage the licensed operator staffing pipeline and leadership succession. A healthy pipeline keeps the control room staffed with qualified, licensed crews.

skills.name: Event Response Leadership
skills.description: You lead the operations response to significant plant events and drive the resulting improvements. Your leadership turns events into lasting reductions in risk.

roles.description: You are the senior leader accountable for the entire operations department and the safe operation of the plant across all shifts. You set standards, manage operational risk, and own the licensed operator pipeline, ensuring crews are staffed, qualified, and performing conservatively. As the top operations authority, you carry ultimate departmental responsibility for protecting the core and the public.

roles.title: Radiation Protection Technician
roles.degree_detail: Many technicians enter with a two year associate degree in radiation protection or nuclear technology, though some start from a high school diploma plus utility or Navy nuclear training. You complete site specific RP qualification and NRC or vendor training. The National Registry of Radiation Protection Technologists (NRRPT) credential is the common professional benchmark earned after field experience.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years, or a military nuclear or health physics background; strong outage and overtime earnings common at commercial plants

skills.name: Radiological Survey Technique
skills.description: You perform contamination, dose rate, and smear surveys using Geiger-Mueller probes, ion chambers, and portable friskers. You interpret counts per minute against release limits and document results on survey maps.

skills.name: Radiation Work Permit Coverage
skills.description: You brief and cover workers under a Radiation Work Permit, verifying stay times, dose budgets, and protective clothing. You stop work when conditions change beyond permit limits.

skills.name: Personnel Contamination Control
skills.description: You operate personnel contamination monitors and portal monitors at step-off pads and controlled area exits. You direct decontamination and process skin dose assessments when alarms occur.

skills.name: Dosimetry Use and Control
skills.description: You issue, read, and troubleshoot electronic dosimeters and TLD or OSL badges. You set dose and dose rate alarm setpoints appropriate to the radiological job scope.

skills.name: Radioactive Material Handling
skills.description: You tag, survey, and control radioactive material and sources, maintaining chain of custody and posting high radiation and contaminated areas per 10 CFR 20.

skills.name: ALARA Field Practice
skills.description: You apply time, distance, and shielding to keep worker dose as low as reasonably achievable. You position temporary lead shielding and recommend job sequencing to cut collective exposure.

roles.description: You are the frontline radiation protection presence at a commercial plant, research reactor, or industrial site. You survey work areas, cover radiologically significant tasks, control contamination, and keep worker dose low. You are often the first to detect changing radiological conditions and are trusted to halt work to protect people.

roles.title: Junior Radiation Protection Technician
roles.degree_detail: This role is accessible with a high school diploma or equivalent, and a two year technical degree or military nuclear experience strengthens your start. You complete employer RP fundamentals training and an initial qualification program. With field hours you become eligible to sit for the NRRPT examination.
roles.experience: 0 to 1 year; typically completing initial RP qualification and working under direct oversight of qualified technicians

skills.name: Basic Survey Instrument Operation
skills.description: You source check and operate friskers, teletectors, and ion chambers before field use. You recognize instrument failure or off scale readings and report them immediately.

skills.name: Controlled Area Posting
skills.description: You install and verify radiological postings, barricades, and boundary ropes for radiation, contamination, and airborne areas. You keep postings current as conditions change.

skills.name: Protective Clothing and PPE
skills.description: You stage, don, and doff anti contamination clothing and respiratory protection correctly. You help workers dress out to avoid cross contamination of clean areas.

skills.name: Smear and Swipe Counting
skills.description: You collect removable contamination smears and process them in low background count room instruments. You log results and flag readings above release criteria.

skills.name: Radiological Housekeeping
skills.description: You control contaminated tools, waste, and water, bagging and tagging material for the radwaste stream. You maintain clean step-off pads and contamination control envelopes.

skills.name: Radiation Safety Communication
skills.description: You relay radiological conditions clearly to workers and senior technicians by radio and in briefings. You escalate unexpected alarms or dose rates without delay.

roles.description: You are learning the radiation protection trade under the direction of qualified technicians. You handle postings, instrument source checks, smear counting, and contamination control while completing your initial qualification card. You build the field judgment needed to cover radiological work independently.

roles.title: Decontamination Technician
roles.degree_detail: A high school diploma plus employer radiation worker and decon training is the typical entry path, and an associate degree in nuclear or RP technology helps. You qualify on contamination control and respiratory protection. Experienced decon technicians often progress toward full RP technician qualification and the NRRPT credential.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years; outage heavy schedule with significant overtime during refueling and decommissioning campaigns

skills.name: Surface Decontamination
skills.description: You remove fixed and loose contamination from tools, components, and surfaces using strippable coatings, scrubbing, and chemical methods. You resurvey to confirm levels meet free release or reuse criteria.

skills.name: Contamination Control Envelopes
skills.description: You erect containments, glove bags, and HEPA ventilation to confine airborne and loose contamination during decon. You maintain negative pressure and monitor for breaches.

skills.name: Radwaste Segregation
skills.description: You sort, characterize, and package contaminated waste by activity and classification for the radwaste program. You minimize waste volume to control disposal cost and dose.

skills.name: Personnel Decontamination Support
skills.description: You assist with skin and clothing decontamination at contamination monitors, using gentle methods to avoid abrading skin. You document decon steps and residual activity.

skills.name: Hot Spot Identification
skills.description: You locate elevated dose rate hot spots on piping and components with survey instruments. You flag them for shielding or flushing to reduce job dose.

skills.name: Decon Chemistry Awareness
skills.description: You handle decon chemicals safely, understanding their reaction with activated corrosion products and crud. You coordinate with chemistry on waste water processing.

roles.description: You restore contaminated components, tools, and areas to usable or releasable condition during outages and decommissioning. You build and maintain containments, run HEPA ventilation, and package radwaste while keeping your own dose low. Your work directly lowers plant contamination levels and collective exposure.

roles.title: Dosimetry Clerk
roles.degree_detail: A high school diploma is the minimum, and an associate degree in a technical or records management field is preferred. You train on the site dosimetry software, 10 CFR 20 recordkeeping requirements, and NVLAP dosimeter handling. The role is a common entry point into health physics support and can lead toward technician or dosimetry specialist work.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years; administrative dosimetry role supporting the health physics and access control organization

skills.name: Dosimeter Issue and Tracking
skills.description: You issue, collect, and track TLD, OSL, and electronic dosimeters for workers and visitors. You maintain accurate assignment records tied to each badged individual.

skills.name: Dose Record Management
skills.description: You enter and reconcile occupational dose records in the site dosimetry database. You ensure lifetime and annual dose totals comply with 10 CFR 20 limits.

skills.name: NVLAP Processor Coordination
skills.description: You ship and receive dosimeters to and from the NVLAP accredited processing vendor. You verify reported doses and investigate anomalous or lost badge results.

skills.name: Radiation Worker Records
skills.description: You verify prior employer dose history on NRC Form 4 and current exposure on Form 5. You confirm training and bioassay status before access is granted.

skills.name: Bioassay Scheduling Support
skills.description: You schedule whole body counts and urinalysis bioassay and track completion. You route results to the health physicist for internal dose assessment.

skills.name: Dosimetry Reporting and Audit
skills.description: You compile dose reports for regulators, workers, and management and prepare records for audit. You protect the confidentiality of personal exposure information.

roles.description: You keep the occupational dosimetry program accurate and auditable. You issue and track dosimeters, maintain dose records, coordinate with the NVLAP processing vendor, and support bioassay scheduling. Your records are the legal basis for demonstrating that workers stay within regulatory dose limits.

roles.title: Radiation Protection Instrument Technician
roles.degree_detail: An associate degree in electronics, instrumentation, or radiation protection technology is the typical foundation, sometimes paired with military nuclear instrument experience. You train on calibration standards, NIST traceability, and the specific detector systems in use. Experienced instrument technicians often pursue the NRRPT credential and can specialize in count room or calibration lab roles.
roles.experience: 0 to 3 years; calibration lab and field instrument support, often blending electronics and RP skills

skills.name: Instrument Calibration
skills.description: You calibrate portable survey meters and friskers against traceable sources in a calibration facility. You document calibration factors and NIST traceability for each instrument.

skills.name: Source Check and Response
skills.description: You perform daily source response and battery checks on field instruments. You tag out of service any meter that fails response or constancy criteria.

skills.name: Count Room Instrument Support
skills.description: You maintain low background alpha and beta counters, liquid scintillation counters, and gamma spectroscopy systems. You run quality control standards and track detector efficiency and background.

skills.name: Area and Continuous Monitors
skills.description: You install, test, and maintain area radiation monitors and continuous air monitors. You set alarm setpoints and troubleshoot false alarms and detector drift.

skills.name: Calibration Source Control
skills.description: You inventory, leak test, and secure sealed calibration and check sources per NRC license conditions. You maintain source accountability records.

skills.name: Instrument Troubleshooting
skills.description: You diagnose electronic and detector faults in RP instrumentation down to the component or module level. You return instruments to service after repair verification.

roles.description: You keep the radiation protection instrument fleet accurate and ready. You calibrate survey meters, maintain count room and air monitoring systems, and control calibration sources under the site license. Reliable instruments depend on your calibrations, so every dose and contamination measurement at the facility traces back to your work.

roles.title: Environmental Monitoring Technician
roles.degree_detail: An associate degree in environmental science, radiation protection, or a related technical field is the common entry point. You train on REMP procedures, chain of custody, and sampling equipment. With experience you can move into environmental monitoring specialist or radiochemistry roles, and the NRRPT credential supports advancement.
roles.experience: 0 to 3 years; field sampling for the radiological environmental monitoring program at a plant, lab, or research reactor

skills.name: Environmental Sample Collection
skills.description: You collect air, water, soil, vegetation, and milk samples at fixed monitoring stations around the facility. You follow chain of custody and sampling frequency required by the REMP.

skills.name: Air Sampling Operation
skills.description: You maintain low volume and high volume air samplers and change particulate and charcoal media on schedule. You record flow rates and total sampled volume for dose calculations.

skills.name: TLD Station Monitoring
skills.description: You service environmental TLD stations at the site boundary and offsite locations. You exchange dosimeters and document direct radiation readings for the public dose assessment.

skills.name: Effluent Pathway Awareness
skills.description: You understand liquid and gaseous effluent release pathways and the critical receptors they reach. You position samples to confirm doses to the public stay below 10 CFR 50 Appendix I limits.

skills.name: Field Data Documentation
skills.description: You log sampling times, weather, and station conditions accurately for defensible environmental records. You flag unusual field observations to the environmental specialist.

skills.name: Low Level Sample Handling
skills.description: You preserve and transfer environmental samples to the radiochemistry lab without cross contamination. You handle low activity media carefully to protect detection sensitivity.

roles.description: You run the field side of the Radiological Environmental Monitoring Program. You collect air, water, soil, vegetation, and TLD samples around the site and deliver them to the counting lab. Your sampling demonstrates to regulators and the public that facility operations have no measurable radiological impact on the environment.

roles.title: Senior Radiation Protection Technician
roles.degree_detail: You typically hold a two year RP or nuclear technology degree plus the NRRPT credential, built on years of qualified field experience. You maintain advanced site qualifications for high radiation and airborne work. Many senior technicians pursue additional ALARA, respiratory protection, or RP supervisor training to move into planning or leadership roles.
roles.experience: 5 to 10 years of qualified RP technician work, including multiple outages and high dose rate job coverage

skills.name: High Risk Job Coverage
skills.description: You provide RP coverage for the highest dose and contamination jobs such as reactor head work, steam generator access, and fuel moves. You make real time judgment calls to protect workers and limit collective dose.

skills.name: RWP and ALARA Planning
skills.description: You author Radiation Work Permits and pre job ALARA reviews for complex evolutions. You set dose budgets, hold points, and contingency actions for changing conditions.

skills.name: Airborne Radioactivity Control
skills.description: You assess airborne radioactivity, derived air concentration, and respiratory protection needs. You determine when containments, ventilation, or respirators are required.

skills.name: Internal Dose Triage
skills.description: You recognize potential uptakes and intakes, initiate bioassay, and brief the health physicist. You take immediate protective actions after a contamination event.

skills.name: Junior Technician Mentoring
skills.description: You coach and qualify junior and new RP technicians in the field. You verify their survey technique and decision making before they cover work alone.

skills.name: Radiological Incident Response
skills.description: You lead the RP response to spills, alarms, and unexpected dose rates. You reconstruct events and recommend corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

roles.description: You are a lead technician trusted with the plant's most radiologically significant work. You plan and cover high dose jobs, write RWPs, control airborne hazards, and respond to radiological events. You set the standard for field RP practice and develop the next generation of technicians.

roles.title: Health Physicist
roles.degree_detail: You hold a bachelor's degree in health physics, physics, nuclear engineering, or radiological science, and many health physicists pursue a master's degree. You build experience toward the American Board of Health Physics certification. Early certification milestones such as passing Part I of the ABHP exam mark progress toward the Certified Health Physicist credential.
roles.experience: 2 to 6 years applying health physics at a plant, national lab, hospital, or research reactor

skills.name: Dose Assessment and Modeling
skills.description: You calculate external and internal dose using exposure data, bioassay, and intake models such as ICRP methods. You assign committed effective dose after contamination or uptake events.

skills.name: Shielding Design
skills.description: You perform shielding calculations with point kernel and Monte Carlo tools such as MicroShield or MCNP. You specify shielding for sources, shipments, and radiation generating equipment.

skills.name: Radiological Hazard Analysis
skills.description: You evaluate new work, sources, and facility changes for radiological hazards. You set controls, postings, and monitoring requirements to keep dose within limits.

skills.name: Regulatory Compliance
skills.description: You interpret 10 CFR 20 and applicable state and NRC requirements for the radiation protection program. You prepare compliance documentation and support inspections.

skills.name: Air Sampling and Dispersion
skills.description: You design air sampling strategies and model airborne dispersion for releases and confined work. You determine derived air concentration and respiratory protection needs.

skills.name: Counting Lab Interpretation
skills.description: You interpret gamma spectroscopy, alpha, and beta results and judge minimum detectable activity. You translate counting data into dose and release decisions.

roles.description: You are the technical radiation safety expert who turns physics into practical controls. You calculate dose, design shielding, analyze hazards, and interpret counting and air sampling data across operational and emergency situations. You advise technicians, engineers, and management on how to keep radiation exposure safe and compliant.

roles.title: ALARA Engineer
roles.degree_detail: You typically hold a bachelor's degree in nuclear engineering, health physics, or a related discipline, and senior RP technicians with strong analytical skills also fill this role. You train on dose modeling, source term chemistry, and ALARA program standards. Many ALARA engineers work toward health physics certification or professional engineering licensure.
roles.experience: 3 to 7 years in radiation protection or nuclear engineering with dose reduction focus

skills.name: Collective Dose Planning
skills.description: You forecast and track collective dose in person rem for outages and major projects. You build dose estimates by job and drive work scope toward the lowest achievable exposure.

skills.name: Source Term Reduction
skills.description: You analyze plant chemistry, crud, and activated corrosion products that drive dose rates. You recommend zinc injection, decontamination, and chemistry controls to lower source term.

skills.name: Shielding and Mockup Strategy
skills.description: You plan temporary shielding packages and full scale mockups for high dose jobs. You optimize placement to cut dose rate while preserving access and schedule.

skills.name: ALARA Review Facilitation
skills.description: You lead pre job and post job ALARA reviews with work crews and RP. You capture lessons learned and feed them into future dose estimates.

skills.name: Dose Tracking Analytics
skills.description: You use dose tracking software and electronic dosimetry data to monitor jobs against budget in real time. You intervene when a job trends over its planned exposure.

skills.name: Industry Benchmarking
skills.description: You benchmark site dose performance against INPO and industry data. You apply best practices from operating experience to continuously lower exposure.

roles.description: You own the as low as reasonably achievable program and drive down worker exposure. You forecast collective dose, attack source term, plan shielding and mockups, and lead ALARA reviews for major work. Your analysis turns dose reduction from a goal into measurable person rem savings each outage.

roles.title: Radiochemistry Analyst
roles.degree_detail: You hold a bachelor's degree in chemistry, radiochemistry, or a related science, and a master's degree helps for method development roles. You train on specific instruments and radiochemical procedures and work under a laboratory QA program. Experienced analysts can pursue health physics or laboratory accreditation specialties and move into lab supervision.
roles.experience: 2 to 6 years in a counting or radiochemistry laboratory at a plant, national lab, or commercial lab

skills.name: Gamma Spectroscopy
skills.description: You identify and quantify gamma emitting radionuclides using high purity germanium detectors and spectral analysis software. You resolve peaks, correct for interferences, and report activity with uncertainty.

skills.name: Radiochemical Separation
skills.description: You perform wet chemistry separations for hard to detect nuclides such as strontium 90, technetium 99, and transuranics. You purify samples to isolate the nuclide before counting.

skills.name: Alpha Spectrometry
skills.description: You prepare samples by electrodeposition and analyze alpha emitters such as isotopes of uranium, plutonium, and americium. You track tracer recovery and chemical yield.

skills.name: Liquid Scintillation Counting
skills.description: You measure beta emitters such as tritium and carbon 14 by liquid scintillation. You control quench and background to maintain low detection limits.

skills.name: Minimum Detectable Activity Control
skills.description: You calculate and defend minimum detectable activity for each method and matrix. You optimize count time and sample size to meet effluent and environmental detection requirements.

skills.name: Laboratory Quality Assurance
skills.description: You run calibration standards, blanks, and spikes and maintain NELAP or equivalent QA records. You participate in interlaboratory comparison programs to prove accuracy.

roles.description: You produce the defensible radionuclide measurements that effluent, environmental, and dose programs rely on. You run gamma spectroscopy, radiochemical separations, alpha spectrometry, and liquid scintillation counting while holding tight quality control. Your low detection limits confirm that releases and environmental samples stay well below regulatory thresholds.

roles.title: Environmental Monitoring Specialist
roles.degree_detail: You hold a bachelor's degree in health physics, environmental science, or a related field, and a master's degree is common for the dose modeling work. You train on the Offsite Dose Calculation Manual, effluent regulations, and environmental transport codes. Many specialists pursue the Certified Health Physicist credential to advance into program leadership.
roles.experience: 3 to 7 years in radiological environmental or effluent monitoring programs

skills.name: REMP Program Management
skills.description: You manage the Radiological Environmental Monitoring Program sampling design, stations, and schedule. You ensure sampling pathways and locations match the Offsite Dose Calculation Manual.

skills.name: Effluent Dose Calculation
skills.description: You calculate offsite dose from liquid and gaseous effluent releases per 10 CFR 50 Appendix I. You verify releases stay within technical specification and permit limits.

skills.name: Environmental Dose Modeling
skills.description: You model atmospheric and aquatic transport to critical receptors and age groups. You estimate dose through inhalation, ingestion, and direct radiation pathways.

skills.name: Annual Radiological Reporting
skills.description: You prepare the Annual Radiological Environmental Operating Report and effluent release report for the NRC. You explain trends, anomalies, and land use census changes.

skills.name: Land Use Census
skills.description: You conduct land use and demographic surveys to identify the nearest residence, garden, and dairy. You update the dose model when critical receptors shift.

skills.name: Interlaboratory Comparison
skills.description: You run the environmental lab through cross check and split sample programs to prove data quality. You investigate and resolve any discrepant results.

roles.description: You demonstrate that the facility has no measurable radiological impact on the public or environment. You design the REMP, calculate effluent doses, model environmental transport, and author the annual regulatory reports. Your work is the public facing proof that operations keep offsite dose far below regulatory limits.

roles.title: Radiation Safety Officer
roles.degree_detail: RSO positions usually require a graduate degree in health physics or a related field, or a bachelor's degree with extensive experience, plus formal RSO training recognized by the NRC or the Agreement State. The Texas Department of State Health Services names the RSO on the license. Many RSOs hold the Certified Health Physicist credential, which strengthens regulatory and professional standing.
roles.experience: 8 or more years in health physics or radiation protection, with named RSO authority on an NRC or Agreement State license

skills.name: Radioactive Materials Licensing
skills.description: You hold named RSO authority on the NRC or Texas Agreement State license and manage its conditions. You submit amendments, renewals, and respond to regulatory correspondence.

skills.name: Radiation Safety Program Oversight
skills.description: You direct the full radiation safety program covering sources, machines, dosimetry, and training. You hold authority to restrict or stop radiological operations that are unsafe.

skills.name: Regulatory Inspection Management
skills.description: You host NRC and state inspectors and lead the response to findings and violations. You develop corrective action plans and track them to closure.

skills.name: Source and Machine Control
skills.description: You maintain inventory, leak testing, and security of sealed sources and radiation generating machines. You enforce controls required for increased controls and security of category 1 and 2 sources.

skills.name: Incident and Overexposure Response
skills.description: You investigate lost sources, overexposures, and contamination events and make required regulatory notifications. You lead root cause analysis and report to management and regulators.

skills.name: Radiation Safety Committee Leadership
skills.description: You chair or advise the radiation safety committee on policy, authorized users, and new uses of radiation. You balance operational needs against regulatory and ALARA obligations.

roles.description: You are the legally accountable authority for radiation safety at a hospital, university, research reactor, or industrial licensee. You hold RSO authority on the license, direct the program, manage regulatory inspections, and control all sources and machines. You have the standing to stop any radiological activity that threatens safety or compliance.

roles.title: Health Physics Manager
roles.degree_detail: You typically hold a graduate degree in health physics, nuclear engineering, or physics and the Certified Health Physicist credential from the American Board of Health Physics. You have a long record of operational health physics and demonstrated leadership. Continuing certification maintenance and management training keep you current in both the science and the organization.
roles.experience: 10 or more years in health physics with team leadership and budget accountability

skills.name: Health Physics Team Leadership
skills.description: You lead health physicists, dosimetrists, and technical staff across operational and project work. You set technical standards and develop staff qualifications and succession.

skills.name: Program Budget and Staffing
skills.description: You own the health physics budget, staffing plan, and outage augmentation. You balance dose reduction investment against operational cost and schedule.

skills.name: Technical Decision Authority
skills.description: You make final technical calls on dose assessments, shielding, and hazard controls. You defend those decisions to senior management and regulators.

skills.name: Dosimetry Program Governance
skills.description: You govern the NVLAP accredited dosimetry program and internal dose assessment methods. You ensure dose of record is accurate, legally defensible, and compliant with 10 CFR 20.

skills.name: Emergency Response Dose Assessment
skills.description: You lead the dose assessment function in the emergency plan, projecting offsite dose during events. You advise on protective action recommendations to decision makers.

skills.name: Regulatory and Industry Interface
skills.description: You represent the organization to the NRC, INPO, and industry groups on health physics matters. You translate operating experience into program improvements.

roles.description: You lead the health physics organization and own its technical and personnel performance. You direct a team of physicists and dosimetrists, control the budget, make the final technical calls, and govern the dosimetry program. You are the health physics voice in emergency response and in dealings with regulators and industry.

roles.title: Radiation Protection Program Manager
roles.degree_detail: This role usually calls for a graduate degree in health physics or nuclear engineering, or a bachelor's degree with extensive senior RP experience. A background that includes the NRRPT credential and progression through technician and supervisory ranks is common and valued. The Certified Health Physicist credential and utility leadership development programs support the move into program management.
roles.experience: 10 or more years in commercial nuclear RP, including outage and department leadership

skills.name: RP Program Ownership
skills.description: You own the site radiation protection program and its governing procedures and technical specifications. You ensure the program meets 10 CFR 20, the license, and INPO standards.

skills.name: Outage RP Leadership
skills.description: You lead radiation protection for refueling outages, directing dozens of technicians and contractors. You set the collective dose goal and drive the schedule without compromising safety.

skills.name: Performance Indicator Management
skills.description: You track RP performance indicators such as dose, contamination events, and personnel contaminations. You drive corrective action when indicators trend adversely.

skills.name: Nuclear Safety Culture
skills.description: You reinforce a strong nuclear safety culture and a questioning attitude in the RP organization. You protect the right of any worker to stop radiologically unsafe work.

skills.name: Corrective Action Program
skills.description: You use the corrective action program to resolve RP deficiencies and operating experience. You hold the organization accountable for timely, effective fixes.

skills.name: Regulatory and INPO Readiness
skills.description: You prepare the RP organization for NRC inspections and INPO evaluations. You close gaps against regulatory and industry excellence standards.

roles.description: You are the senior leader accountable for radiation protection at a commercial nuclear plant. You own the RP program, lead it through outages, manage performance indicators, and drive a strong safety culture. You answer to plant management, the NRC, and INPO for how well the station protects its workers from radiation.

roles.title: Certified Health Physicist, Technical Lead
roles.degree_detail: You hold a graduate degree in health physics or a closely related field and the Certified Health Physicist credential from the American Board of Health Physics, earned by passing both parts of a rigorous examination. You maintain certification through continuing education and professional contribution. Active participation in the Health Physics Society and standards committees keeps you at the leading edge of the field.
roles.experience: 10 or more years in health physics holding the ABHP certification; recognized technical authority

skills.name: Advanced Dose Reconstruction
skills.description: You reconstruct complex internal and external doses from incomplete data using ICRP biokinetic models. You defend committed dose assignments in legal and regulatory settings.

skills.name: Monte Carlo Shielding Analysis
skills.description: You perform advanced shielding and dose analysis with MCNP or similar transport codes. You validate models against measurements for high consequence applications.

skills.name: Technical Peer Review
skills.description: You peer review dose assessments, shielding designs, and safety analyses across the organization. You catch errors and raise the technical rigor of health physics products.

skills.name: Regulatory Standard Development
skills.description: You contribute to ANSI, HPS, and NRC regulatory guide development on radiation protection. You interpret evolving standards for your organization.

skills.name: Complex Decommissioning Analysis
skills.description: You develop derived concentration guideline levels and final status survey designs for decommissioning. You apply MARSSIM methods to demonstrate sites meet release criteria.

skills.name: Expert Consultation and Mentoring
skills.description: You serve as the final technical authority on radiation protection questions. You mentor junior health physicists toward board certification.

roles.description: You are the recognized technical authority in health physics, the person others turn to for the hardest problems. You reconstruct complex doses, run advanced shielding models, lead decommissioning analyses, and peer review the organization's most important work. You shape standards and mentor the next generation of certified health physicists.

roles.title: Radiation Protection Superintendent
roles.degree_detail: You usually hold a bachelor's degree in a technical field, though many superintendents rise from the technician ranks with an associate degree and the NRRPT credential plus extensive experience. You complete utility supervisory and RP leadership training and maintain senior RP qualifications. Further graduate study or health physics certification supports a move into program manager or health physics manager roles.
roles.experience: 12 or more years in commercial nuclear RP, progressing from technician through supervisor to department management

skills.name: RP Department Supervision
skills.description: You supervise RP shift supervisors, technicians, and support staff across operating and outage conditions. You set work priorities, approve qualifications, and manage discipline and performance.

skills.name: Radiological Work Authorization
skills.description: You approve high risk Radiation Work Permits and authorize entries into high and very high radiation areas. You verify dose budgets and controls before work proceeds.

skills.name: Collective Dose Accountability
skills.description: You are accountable for site collective dose and personnel contamination performance. You drive ALARA goals through the department and hold crews to the dose plan.

skills.name: Outage RP Execution
skills.description: You direct day to day RP execution during refueling outages, coordinating augmented staff and contractor technicians. You resolve emergent radiological problems to keep the schedule safe and on track.

skills.name: Procedure and Qualification Governance
skills.description: You own RP procedures and the technician qualification program. You ensure training and requalification meet regulatory and INPO expectations.

skills.name: Management and Regulatory Interface
skills.description: You brief plant management on radiological status and risk and support NRC inspections. You translate regulatory requirements into field level direction for the department.

roles.description: You run the day to day radiation protection department at a commercial plant, bridging technician execution and program management. You supervise RP staff, approve high risk work, own collective dose performance, and lead outage execution. When radiological problems arise in the field, the decision to proceed or stop ultimately rests with you.

roles.title: Licensing Analyst
roles.degree_detail: A four year bachelor's degree in nuclear, mechanical, or electrical engineering is the common path, though degrees in physics, chemistry, or a regulatory or policy field are accepted. Coursework in reactor systems and technical writing helps. Many analysts enter directly from an engineering program and learn the licensing basis on the job.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years in nuclear, engineering, or regulatory support; internship or co-op in a utility licensing group is a plus.

skills.name: 10 CFR 50 and 52 Familiarity
skills.description: You learn how the operating license and combined license frameworks under 10 CFR 50 and 52 govern plant activities. You trace which license condition or Technical Specification applies to a proposed change.

skills.name: License Basis Research
skills.description: You search the Updated Final Safety Analysis Report, Technical Specifications, and NRC correspondence to locate the current licensing basis for a system or activity. You compile accurate references for senior licensing staff.

skills.name: Regulatory Document Tracking
skills.description: You track NRC Requests for Additional Information, generic letters, and bulletins against internal due dates. You keep the licensing action log current so nothing slips past a committed response date.

skills.name: Technical Writing
skills.description: You draft clear, defensible sections of license amendment requests and no significant hazards consideration write-ups. You cite the specific regulation or Technical Specification that supports each statement.

skills.name: ADAMS and Docket Navigation
skills.description: You retrieve dockets, inspection reports, and precedent amendments from the NRC ADAMS system. You find prior approvals that strengthen a current submittal.

skills.name: Change Screening Support
skills.description: You assist engineers in gathering inputs for 10 CFR 50.59 screenings and evaluations. You confirm whether a change touches the UFSAR or a Technical Specification before it advances.

roles.description: You support the licensing group by researching the plant licensing basis and drafting pieces of regulatory submittals. You keep license amendment requests, RAI responses, and commitment tracking organized and on schedule. You build the regulatory foundation that senior licensing engineers rely on to interface with the NRC.

roles.title: QA Inspector
roles.degree_detail: A two year associate degree in a quality, mechanical, or nondestructive testing technology program is typical, and some inspectors enter from a skilled trade or military nuclear background. Employer sponsored qualification to Appendix B inspection procedures and ANSI standards follows hire. Nondestructive examination certifications expand the roles you can cover.
roles.experience: 0 to 3 years in quality inspection, manufacturing, or a skilled trade; nuclear or ASME code environment experience preferred.

skills.name: Appendix B Inspection
skills.description: You perform receipt and in-process inspections against the 10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality program. You verify that safety related components meet drawing, specification, and procedure requirements before acceptance.

skills.name: Measurement and Test Equipment
skills.description: You use calibrated gauges, micrometers, and test equipment and confirm each tool is within its calibration interval. You record readings accurately and reject out of tolerance items.

skills.name: Nonconformance Documentation
skills.description: You write nonconformance reports when a component fails to meet requirements. You describe the condition clearly so engineering can disposition it under the corrective action program.

skills.name: Inspection Records
skills.description: You complete inspection reports, travelers, and quality records that become part of the permanent plant record. You ensure signatures, dates, and hold points are satisfied before release.

skills.name: Code and Standard Reading
skills.description: You read ASME Section III, procurement specifications, and inspection procedures to know the acceptance criteria. You apply the correct hold and witness points for each item.

skills.name: Material Traceability
skills.description: You verify heat numbers, certified material test reports, and part markings to maintain traceability of safety related material. You catch missing or mismatched documentation before installation.

roles.description: You inspect safety related components, materials, and work against the Appendix B quality program and applicable codes. You document conformance, flag nonconforming items, and protect the integrity of the plant's quality records. You are a first line defense against defective material reaching safety related systems.

roles.title: Document Control Specialist
