roles.degree_detail: A two year associate degree in information management, business, or a technical field is common, and a high school diploma with strong records experience can be enough. Training in the plant document management system and ANSI N45.2.9 records standards is provided after hire. Some specialists move up from administrative roles within the utility.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years in records management, document control, or administrative support, preferably in a regulated industry.

skills.name: Controlled Document Management
skills.description: You issue, revise, and retire controlled documents such as procedures, drawings, and calculations under configuration control. You make sure only the current approved revision is available to users.

skills.name: Quality Records Retention
skills.description: You handle lifetime and nonpermanent quality records per the Appendix B records program and ANSI N45.2.9. You store, index, and protect records so they are retrievable for the life of the plant.

skills.name: Electronic Document Systems
skills.description: You operate the plant electronic document management system to route documents for review, approval, and release. You maintain accurate metadata so records can be found by document number or system.

skills.name: Revision and Change Control
skills.description: You process revision requests and verify that superseded copies are removed from use. You keep the master index aligned with the configuration of record.

skills.name: Records Audit Readiness
skills.description: You prepare records packages for NRC inspections, INPO evaluations, and internal audits. You confirm completeness and legibility before a package leaves the vault.

skills.name: Confidentiality and Security
skills.description: You handle safeguards information and proprietary vendor documents under the correct access controls. You follow information handling rules so sensitive records are not released improperly.

roles.description: You control the plant's regulated documents and quality records so the right revision reaches the right person every time. You index, retain, and retrieve records that must survive for the life of the plant and satisfy NRC and Appendix B requirements. You keep the configuration of record accurate and audit ready.

roles.title: Compliance Coordinator
roles.degree_detail: A four year bachelor's degree in business, engineering, a science, or a regulatory or policy field is typical. Some coordinators enter with an associate degree plus strong compliance or administrative experience. On the job training covers the station commitment management and corrective action systems.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years in compliance, regulatory support, or administration; nuclear or utility experience preferred.

skills.name: Commitment Tracking
skills.description: You maintain the regulatory commitment database so every promise made to the NRC has an owner and a due date. You alert responsible managers before a commitment comes due.

skills.name: License Condition Monitoring
skills.description: You monitor compliance with license conditions, Technical Specifications, and the Operating License. You flag any activity that drifts outside an approved requirement.

skills.name: Reporting Deadline Management
skills.description: You track reportable event clocks such as the Licensee Event Report timeliness requirements of 10 CFR 50.72 and 50.73. You coordinate inputs so reports reach the NRC within the required window.

skills.name: Procedure Compliance Support
skills.description: You help confirm that station procedures reflect current regulatory requirements. You route gaps to the owning department for revision under the change process.

skills.name: Audit and Inspection Logistics
skills.description: You schedule and organize the material for NRC inspections and internal audits. You make sure requested documents and interviewees are ready on time.

skills.name: Regulatory Correspondence Handling
skills.description: You log incoming NRC correspondence and route it to the correct action owner. You maintain an accurate record of commitments and responses in the correspondence system.

roles.description: You keep the station's regulatory commitments, license conditions, and reporting deadlines organized and visible. You coordinate the logistics of NRC inspections and internal audits and route regulatory correspondence to the right owners. You help the plant demonstrate that it does what it told the regulator it would do.

roles.title: Records and Configuration Clerk
roles.degree_detail: A two year associate degree in office administration, information management, or a technical field is typical, and some clerks enter with a high school diploma and relevant experience. Employer training covers the records management system, retention standards, and configuration management basics. This role is a common entry point into document control and configuration management careers.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years in records, data entry, or clerical work; experience with drawing or configuration systems is a plus.

skills.name: Drawing and Configuration Records
skills.description: You maintain controlled drawings, piping and instrumentation diagrams, and equipment records that define the plant configuration. You verify that as built changes are reflected in the configuration of record.

skills.name: Data Entry Accuracy
skills.description: You enter equipment, document, and change data into plant databases with high accuracy. You check your entries against source documents to prevent configuration errors.

skills.name: Change Package Processing
skills.description: You process modification and change packages through the records workflow. You confirm that all required approvals and attachments are present before closure.

skills.name: Retention Schedule Application
skills.description: You apply the correct retention category to each record under the quality records program. You keep lifetime quality records protected and retrievable.

skills.name: Index and Retrieval
skills.description: You index records so they can be located quickly during inspections and engineering work. You respond to retrieval requests accurately and promptly.

skills.name: Physical and Electronic Filing
skills.description: You maintain both physical record vaults and electronic repositories under configuration control. You keep storage conditions and access logs compliant with program requirements.

roles.description: You keep the plant's configuration and quality records accurate, protected, and retrievable. You process change packages, apply retention rules, and index records so engineers and auditors can find them. You support the configuration management program that ties the physical plant to its documentation.

roles.title: Regulatory Affairs Associate
roles.degree_detail: A four year bachelor's degree in engineering, a physical science, political science, or a related field is typical, with strong emphasis on research and writing. Some associates hold a law, policy, or public administration background. On the job mentoring builds knowledge of the NRC regulatory framework and the station licensing basis.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years in regulatory affairs, engineering, or policy; strong writing and research skills expected.

skills.name: NRC Rulemaking Monitoring
skills.description: You monitor Federal Register notices, proposed rules, and NRC generic communications for impacts on the station. You summarize new requirements for the regulatory affairs team.

skills.name: Industry Guidance Research
skills.description: You research NRC Regulatory Guides, NUREGs, and NEI guidance that apply to a given issue. You compile the relevant positions to support a regulatory strategy.

skills.name: Correspondence Drafting
skills.description: You draft letters and responses to the NRC under the review of senior regulatory affairs staff. You use precise regulatory language and cite the governing requirement.

skills.name: Meeting Support
skills.description: You prepare materials and take accurate notes for public meetings and calls with the NRC. You track action items and follow them to closure.

skills.name: Generic Communication Response
skills.description: You help evaluate bulletins, generic letters, and information notices for applicability. You coordinate the station's formal response where one is required.

skills.name: Regulatory Issue Tracking
skills.description: You maintain a log of open regulatory issues and their status. You keep the team aware of upcoming deadlines and emerging requirements.

roles.description: You track the evolving regulatory landscape and help the station respond to new NRC requirements and generic communications. You research industry guidance, draft correspondence, and support meetings with the regulator. You develop the regulatory judgment that leads toward a regulatory affairs specialist role.

roles.title: Licensing Engineer
roles.degree_detail: A four year bachelor's degree in nuclear, mechanical, electrical, or chemical engineering is standard, and a master's degree can accelerate advancement. A Professional Engineer license is valued but not always required. Deep knowledge comes from years of applying 10 CFR 50.59 and managing the plant licensing basis.
roles.experience: 4 to 8 years in nuclear engineering or licensing, including hands on preparation of license amendments and 50.59 evaluations.

skills.name: 10 CFR 50.59 Evaluations
skills.description: You perform and own 50.59 screenings and evaluations to determine whether a change requires prior NRC approval. You defend your conclusion with the eight evaluation criteria and the licensing basis.

skills.name: License Amendment Requests
skills.description: You prepare complete license amendment requests including the no significant hazards consideration and technical justification. You anticipate NRC questions and address them in the initial submittal.

skills.name: Technical Specification Interpretation
skills.description: You interpret and apply Technical Specifications, including Limiting Conditions for Operation and surveillance requirements. You advise operations on compliance when a condition is challenged.

skills.name: RAI Response
skills.description: You draft responses to NRC Requests for Additional Information that resolve the staff's concern on the first pass. You coordinate engineering inputs into a consistent, defensible answer.

skills.name: Licensing Basis Management
skills.description: You maintain the integrity of the UFSAR and current licensing basis as changes occur. You ensure amendments and 50.59 evaluations feed back into the documents of record.

skills.name: Regulatory Strategy
skills.description: You recommend whether to pursue an amendment, an exemption, or a 50.59 path for a proposed change. You weigh schedule, risk, and precedent to choose the most defensible approach.

roles.description: You own licensing evaluations and amendment requests that keep plant changes within the approved licensing basis. You perform 50.59 evaluations, interpret Technical Specifications, and respond to NRC questions with defensible technical justification. You are the engineer who decides when a change can proceed and when the NRC must approve it first.

roles.title: Regulatory Affairs Specialist
roles.degree_detail: A four year bachelor's degree in engineering, a physical science, or a policy or regulatory field is standard, and a graduate degree in engineering, law, or public administration is common at this level. Experience interfacing with the NRC is essential. Many specialists come up through licensing engineering or operations.
roles.experience: 4 to 9 years in regulatory affairs, licensing, or nuclear engineering with direct NRC interface experience.

skills.name: NRC Interface
skills.description: You serve as a point of contact with NRC project managers and regional staff on assigned issues. You communicate the station's position clearly and maintain a credible, professional relationship.

skills.name: Regulatory Impact Analysis
skills.description: You analyze new rules, orders, and generic communications for their impact on the station. You develop the implementation strategy and schedule to achieve compliance.

skills.name: Reactor Oversight Process Knowledge
skills.description: You apply the NRC Reactor Oversight Process, including performance indicators and the significance determination process. You help interpret inspection findings and color assignments for the station.

skills.name: Exemption and Relief Requests
skills.description: You prepare exemption, relief, and enforcement discretion requests with strong technical and regulatory justification. You build the case that supports NRC approval.

skills.name: Enforcement and Allegation Response
skills.description: You coordinate the station's response to notices of violation and allegations. You assemble the facts and corrective actions that resolve the concern.

skills.name: Industry Engagement
skills.description: You engage with NEI, owners groups, and peer utilities on shared regulatory issues. You bring industry positions and precedent back into the station's strategy.

roles.description: You are the station's working interface with the NRC on regulatory issues, new rules, and oversight process matters. You analyze regulatory impacts, prepare exemption and relief requests, and coordinate responses to findings and allegations. You translate the NRC's expectations into actionable strategy for the plant.

roles.title: Quality Assurance Engineer
roles.degree_detail: A four year bachelor's degree in mechanical, nuclear, materials, or industrial engineering is standard. Professional quality certifications such as the ASQ Certified Quality Engineer and lead auditor qualification strengthen the role. Knowledge of NQA-1 and 10 CFR 50 Appendix B is built through program experience.
roles.experience: 4 to 8 years in nuclear quality assurance, engineering, or supplier quality under an Appendix B program.

skills.name: Appendix B Program Implementation
skills.description: You implement and interpret the 10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality assurance program across the station's eighteen criteria. You ensure design, procurement, and work activities meet quality requirements.

skills.name: Supplier Quality Oversight
skills.description: You evaluate and audit safety related suppliers for compliance with their approved quality programs. You assess commercial grade dedication and the acceptability of procured items.

skills.name: Quality Program Procedures
skills.description: You write and revise quality program procedures and ensure they align with NQA-1 and regulatory requirements. You keep the program current with industry operating experience.

skills.name: Root Cause and Trending
skills.description: You analyze quality trends and support root cause evaluations of quality program deficiencies. You recommend corrective actions that prevent recurrence.

skills.name: Commercial Grade Dedication
skills.description: You evaluate critical characteristics and acceptance methods to dedicate commercial items for safety related use. You document the technical basis under 10 CFR 21 and EPRI guidance.

skills.name: Audit Participation
skills.description: You plan and execute internal and supplier quality audits to NQA-1 and ANSI N45.2.23. You write findings that drive measurable improvement.

roles.description: You implement and sustain the Appendix B quality assurance program across design, procurement, and work activities. You oversee supplier quality, lead commercial grade dedication, and audit against NQA-1 standards. You make sure safety related work and material meet the quality requirements that protect the public.

roles.title: Corrective Action Program Analyst
roles.degree_detail: A four year bachelor's degree in engineering or a physical science is typical, and operations or maintenance experience is highly valued. Formal root cause analysis training and corrective action program qualification follow hire. Many analysts come from the control room, engineering, or maintenance into this role.
roles.experience: 3 to 8 years in nuclear operations, engineering, or quality with hands on corrective action program work.

skills.name: Condition Report Screening
skills.description: You screen condition reports to assign significance, operability impact, and reportability. You make sure emerging issues are classified correctly and routed promptly.

skills.name: Root Cause Analysis
skills.description: You lead and review root cause and apparent cause evaluations using methods such as events and causal factors and barrier analysis. You confirm the real cause is identified, not just the symptom.

skills.name: Corrective Action Effectiveness
skills.description: You develop and track corrective actions to prevent recurrence and verify their effectiveness. You close actions only when evidence shows the problem is resolved.

skills.name: Trending and Common Cause
skills.description: You trend low level issues to detect adverse trends and common cause before they become significant. You present trend data that drives management attention.

skills.name: Operability and Reportability
skills.description: You support operability determinations and reportability assessments under 10 CFR 50.72 and 50.73. You ensure degraded conditions are evaluated against the licensing basis.

skills.name: Operating Experience Integration
skills.description: You screen INPO and industry operating experience for applicability to the station. You create actions that apply external lessons before an event happens here.

roles.description: You run the engine of the corrective action program, from screening condition reports to driving root cause analysis and verifying effectiveness. You trend emerging issues, integrate industry operating experience, and support operability and reportability decisions. You help the station find and fix problems before they challenge safety.

roles.title: Nuclear Oversight Auditor
roles.degree_detail: A four year bachelor's degree in engineering or a technical field is standard, supported by broad station experience in operations, engineering, or quality. Qualification as a lead auditor under ANSI N45.2.23 is required to lead audits. Auditors are often experienced staff who rotate into oversight to apply their plant knowledge.
roles.experience: 5 to 10 years in nuclear operations, engineering, or quality, with qualification as a nuclear auditor.

skills.name: Audit Planning and Execution
skills.description: You plan, lead, and report audits of station programs against regulatory and quality requirements. You gather objective evidence and draw conclusions that hold up to challenge.

skills.name: Independent Oversight
skills.description: You provide independent assessment of station performance separate from line management. You raise issues candidly even when they are unwelcome.

skills.name: Regulatory Compliance Assessment
skills.description: You assess compliance with 10 CFR, Technical Specifications, and the quality assurance program. You verify that the station meets its license and commitments in practice, not just on paper.

skills.name: Observation and Interviewing
skills.description: You observe work in the field and interview personnel to assess behaviors and program health. You distinguish isolated errors from programmatic weaknesses.

skills.name: Finding Development
skills.description: You write audit findings that clearly state the requirement, the condition, and the significance. You enter deficiencies into the corrective action program for resolution.

skills.name: Supplier and Vendor Audits
skills.description: You audit safety related vendors and suppliers to NQA-1 and ANSI N45.2.23. You determine whether a supplier's quality program can be relied upon.

roles.description: You provide independent oversight of station programs, performance, and suppliers through disciplined auditing. You assess compliance with regulations and the quality program, develop findings, and feed deficiencies into corrective action. You are a check on the organization that helps catch weaknesses before the NRC or an event does.

roles.title: Licensing Manager
roles.degree_detail: A four year bachelor's degree in nuclear or a related engineering discipline is required, and a graduate degree in engineering or business is common at this level. A Professional Engineer license and a Senior Reactor Operator certification or instant are valued. The role is reached after a long licensing and engineering career.
roles.experience: 12 or more years in nuclear licensing and engineering, including leadership of license amendment campaigns and NRC interactions.

skills.name: Licensing Program Leadership
skills.description: You lead the station licensing organization and set priorities across amendments, 50.59 evaluations, and commitments. You balance a portfolio of regulatory actions against plant schedules and risk.

skills.name: Licensing Basis Governance
skills.description: You own the integrity of the current licensing basis and the UFSAR for the station. You ensure every change preserves a clear, defensible licensing basis.

skills.name: Senior NRC Engagement
skills.description: You lead high stakes interactions with NRC management on significant licensing actions and issues. You represent the station's position with credibility and transparency.

skills.name: Regulatory Risk Management
skills.description: You assess and manage regulatory risk across major projects such as power uprates and life extension. You guide the station toward strategies that are both achievable and defensible.

skills.name: Team Development
skills.description: You develop licensing engineers and analysts and qualify them in 50.59 and amendment preparation. You build a bench that can carry the station's regulatory workload.

skills.name: Change Process Governance
skills.description: You govern the 10 CFR 50.59 program and the quality of screenings and evaluations stationwide. You hold the line on when NRC approval is required before a change proceeds.

roles.description: You lead the licensing organization that keeps the station operating within its approved licensing basis. You own the UFSAR and licensing basis integrity, lead senior NRC engagements, and manage regulatory risk across major projects. You develop the licensing staff and govern the 50.59 change process for the whole station.

roles.title: Regulatory Affairs Director
roles.degree_detail: A graduate degree in engineering, law, public policy, or business is typical at the director level, built on a four year engineering or science degree. Deep experience interfacing with NRC leadership is essential. Directors are usually seasoned licensing or operations executives with a fleet wide perspective.
roles.experience: 15 or more years in nuclear regulatory affairs, licensing, or operations, with executive level NRC engagement.

skills.name: Regulatory Strategy and Policy
skills.description: You set the fleet or station regulatory strategy and shape positions on emerging NRC policy and rulemaking. You align regulatory posture with long term business and safety goals.

skills.name: Executive NRC Relationships
skills.description: You build and maintain relationships with NRC senior management and regional administrators. You represent the organization in the most consequential regulatory matters.

skills.name: Reactor Oversight Process Strategy
skills.description: You manage the organization's standing in the Reactor Oversight Process and work to keep the station in the licensee response column. You guide the response to findings that could shift the action matrix.

skills.name: Enforcement and Crisis Management
skills.description: You lead the response to significant enforcement actions, special inspections, and regulatory crises. You coordinate legal, technical, and communications resources under pressure.

skills.name: Industry Leadership
skills.description: You represent the organization at NEI and owners groups and influence industry wide regulatory positions. You turn collective industry strategy into advantage for the station.

skills.name: Organizational Governance
skills.description: You govern the licensing, regulatory affairs, and compliance functions as an integrated organization. You ensure resources, processes, and culture support regulatory excellence.

roles.description: You set and own the organization's regulatory strategy and its most senior relationships with the NRC. You manage the station's standing in the Reactor Oversight Process and lead the response to enforcement and regulatory crises. You represent the organization across the industry and govern the licensing, regulatory affairs, and compliance functions.

roles.title: Quality Assurance Manager
roles.degree_detail: A four year bachelor's degree in engineering, materials, or a quality related field is required, and a graduate degree or MBA is common. Senior quality certifications such as the ASQ Certified Manager of Quality and Certified Quality Auditor are valued. The role is reached through years of quality assurance and engineering leadership.
roles.experience: 12 or more years in nuclear quality assurance and engineering, including leadership of an Appendix B program.

skills.name: Quality Program Ownership
skills.description: You own the 10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality assurance program and its description in the licensing basis. You ensure the program meets NQA-1 and remains effective across all safety related activities.

skills.name: Supplier Quality Governance
skills.description: You govern the approved supplier program and the commercial grade dedication process. You decide which suppliers the station can rely on for safety related items.

skills.name: Audit Program Leadership
skills.description: You lead the internal and supplier audit program and ensure findings drive real improvement. You direct audit resources toward the highest risk areas.

skills.name: Regulatory and Code Compliance
skills.description: You ensure compliance with Appendix B, 10 CFR 21, and applicable ASME and NQA-1 requirements. You keep the quality program aligned with evolving regulatory expectations.

skills.name: Quality Culture
skills.description: You build a culture where quality requirements are met and problems are raised early. You hold the organization accountable to the standards the program sets.

skills.name: Program Performance Oversight
skills.description: You monitor quality performance indicators and trends across the station. You report program health candidly to senior management and the NRC.

roles.description: You own the Appendix B quality assurance program and the standards that govern all safety related work and material. You govern supplier quality and commercial grade dedication, lead the audit program, and ensure compliance with NQA-1 and 10 CFR 21. You build the quality culture that keeps the station's safety related activities defect free.

roles.title: Nuclear Safety Culture Lead
roles.degree_detail: A four year bachelor's degree in engineering, a behavioral science, organizational psychology, or a related field is typical, and a graduate degree in human performance or organizational development is common. Broad nuclear experience and credibility with the workforce are essential. Many leads come from operations or oversight backgrounds.
roles.experience: 12 or more years in nuclear operations, oversight, or human performance, with safety culture program leadership.

skills.name: Safety Culture Assessment
skills.description: You lead nuclear safety culture assessments against the NRC safety culture policy statement and INPO traits. You measure the health of the ten traits and identify declining areas.

skills.name: Safety Conscious Work Environment
skills.description: You maintain a safety conscious work environment where staff raise concerns without fear of retaliation. You oversee the employee concerns program and monitor the chilling effect.

skills.name: Human and Organizational Performance
skills.description: You apply human performance and organizational factors analysis to events and trends. You identify latent organizational weaknesses behind recurring issues.

skills.name: Behavioral Trending
skills.description: You trend behaviors, survey results, and condition reports for early signals of culture decline. You bring data based insight to leadership before performance erodes.

skills.name: Leadership Coaching
skills.description: You coach managers and supervisors on the behaviors that reinforce a strong safety culture. You help leaders model questioning attitude and respect for defense in depth.

skills.name: Oversight Integration
skills.description: You integrate safety culture insights with corrective action, oversight, and INPO evaluation results. You connect culture findings to concrete improvement actions.

roles.description: You lead the station's nuclear safety culture program and protect the safety conscious work environment. You assess the INPO traits, oversee the employee concerns program, and apply human and organizational performance analysis. You coach leaders and connect culture insights to oversight and corrective action so the organization stays self critical.

roles.title: NRC Resident Inspector
roles.degree_detail: A four year bachelor's degree in engineering or a physical science is required for the NRC inspector track, and many inspectors hold Senior Reactor Operator experience. New inspectors complete the agency's technical training and qualification program at the Technical Training Center. The role draws on years of prior industry or Navy nuclear experience.
roles.experience: 8 or more years in nuclear engineering, operations, or inspection; federal inspector qualification required.

skills.name: Reactor Oversight Process Inspection
skills.description: You execute the NRC Reactor Oversight Process baseline inspection program at an assigned plant. You apply inspection procedures to verify the licensee meets regulatory requirements.

skills.name: Significance Determination
skills.description: You evaluate inspection findings through the significance determination process to assign a color. You judge the safety significance of a deficiency against established risk criteria.

skills.name: Independent Field Assessment
skills.description: You independently observe operations, maintenance, and engineering work in the plant. You verify compliance with Technical Specifications and the licensing basis firsthand.

skills.name: Licensing Basis Verification
skills.description: You verify that plant configuration and activities remain within the approved licensing basis and 10 CFR requirements. You identify where the licensee has drifted from its license.

skills.name: Violation Documentation
skills.description: You document violations and findings in inspection reports with clear regulatory basis. You communicate concerns to licensee management objectively and firmly.

skills.name: Enforcement Judgment
skills.description: You apply the enforcement policy to determine the appropriate regulatory response to a violation. You balance holding the licensee accountable with encouraging self identification and correction.

roles.description: You are the NRC's eyes on site, executing the Reactor Oversight Process inspection program at an assigned plant. You independently assess operations and engineering, determine the significance of findings, and verify compliance with the licensing basis. You document violations and apply the enforcement policy to protect public health and safety.

roles.title: Safety Analysis Engineer
roles.degree_detail: You need a bachelor of science in nuclear, mechanical, or chemical engineering, or in physics. Coursework in heat transfer, fluid mechanics, and reactor theory is expected. Many employers encourage passing the FE exam early and pursuing a master of science in nuclear engineering while on the job.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years in nuclear engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field; internship or co-op in a nuclear safety organization is a plus.

skills.name: Design-basis accident analysis
skills.description: You run and interpret design-basis transient and accident cases to confirm that acceptance criteria in the plant safety analysis report are met. You document margins to limits such as peak clad temperature and departure from nucleate boiling.

skills.name: RELAP5 input modeling
skills.description: You build and edit RELAP5 thermal-hydraulic nodalization decks for loss-of-coolant and transient scenarios. You check mass and energy balances so your results are defensible.

skills.name: NUREG and regulatory basis
skills.description: You trace analysis requirements back to 10 CFR 50 Appendix K, NUREG-0800 Standard Review Plan sections, and the plant licensing basis. You learn to cite the controlling requirement for every calculation.

skills.name: Engineering calculation control
skills.description: You prepare safety-related calculations under a 10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality program with full traceability of inputs and assumptions. You respond to independent verification and checker comments.

skills.name: Technical specifications literacy
skills.description: You read plant technical specifications to understand the limiting conditions for operation your analysis supports. You connect analytical limits to operability and surveillance requirements.

skills.name: Scientific scripting
skills.description: You use Python or MATLAB to post-process code output, build plots, and automate sensitivity sweeps. You keep scripts documented so reviewers can reproduce your numbers.

roles.description: You support the engineering analyses that demonstrate a reactor meets its design-basis safety requirements. Working under senior analysts, you set up code cases, reduce data, and draft calculation packages for current fleet plants and new SMR projects. You build the regulatory and thermal-hydraulic fundamentals that lead toward licensed analyst work.

roles.title: Junior PRA Engineer
roles.degree_detail: You need a bachelor of science in nuclear, mechanical, electrical, or systems engineering. Coursework in probability, statistics, and reliability is valuable. A master of science focused on reliability or PRA methods strengthens your path toward independent model ownership.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years of experience; exposure to reliability, systems engineering, or probabilistic methods through coursework or internship preferred.

skills.name: Fault tree construction
skills.description: You build and update fault trees for safety systems using CAFTA or SAPHIRE, linking basic events to component failure modes. You check logic against system piping and instrumentation diagrams.

skills.name: Event tree sequencing
skills.description: You model accident sequences from initiating events through to core damage end states. You make sure success criteria and system dependencies are represented correctly.

skills.name: Reliability data application
skills.description: You apply component failure rates and demand probabilities from sources such as NUREG/CR-6928 to basic events. You document data sources and any plant-specific Bayesian updates.

skills.name: PRA software operation
skills.description: You run quantifications in CAFTA or SAPHIRE and extract cutsets, importance measures, and core damage frequency results. You learn to spot non-minimal cutsets and modeling artifacts.

skills.name: System and dependency review
skills.description: You walk down system descriptions to capture support dependencies like power, cooling, and instrument air. You translate those into house events and logic flags.

skills.name: ASME/ANS standard familiarity
skills.description: You learn the supporting requirements of the ASME/ANS PRA Standard RA-Sa and how they drive model technical adequacy. You map your work products to the relevant capability categories.

roles.description: You assist a probabilistic risk assessment team in building and maintaining the plant risk model. You construct fault and event tree logic, apply reliability data, and run quantifications under the guidance of senior PRA engineers. The role is the standard entry path into risk-informed engineering for the operating fleet and advanced reactors.

roles.title: Reactor Physics Analyst
roles.degree_detail: You need a bachelor of science in nuclear engineering with strong coursework in reactor theory, neutron transport, and reactor physics. Hands-on experience with lattice or core simulator codes from a university reactor or internship is valued. A master of science in nuclear engineering is common for advancement into lead physics roles.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years; nuclear engineering coursework in reactor theory and neutronics required.

skills.name: Core neutronics modeling
skills.description: You run lattice and core simulator codes such as CASMO and SIMULATE to generate power distributions and reactivity coefficients. You compare predictions against measured startup physics data.

skills.name: Reactivity coefficient analysis
skills.description: You calculate moderator and fuel temperature coefficients and boron worth to confirm core stability and shutdown margin. You check that values support the safety analysis assumptions.

skills.name: Shutdown margin verification
skills.description: You verify control rod worth and shutdown margin against technical specification limits for each cycle. You document stuck-rod assumptions and their basis.

skills.name: Cross section data handling
skills.description: You manage nuclear cross section libraries and burnup-dependent data used in core models. You confirm the library version matches the licensing basis.

skills.name: Power distribution review
skills.description: You evaluate peaking factors and axial offset against thermal limits to support operability. You flag conditions that approach the limiting values.

skills.name: Core follow and validation
skills.description: You track predicted versus measured core behavior through the cycle to validate the neutronics model. You investigate deviations beyond acceptance bands.

roles.description: You perform neutronics and core physics calculations that feed the reactor safety analysis and support cycle operations. You model power distributions, reactivity coefficients, and shutdown margin, and compare predictions against plant measurements. The role builds the physics foundation used across fuel safety and accident analysis.

roles.title: Criticality Safety Analyst
roles.degree_detail: You need a bachelor of science in nuclear engineering or physics, with coursework in radiation transport, reactor physics, and nuclear criticality safety. Experience with MCNP or SCALE from academic projects is a strong advantage. Many analysts pursue a master of science and specialized criticality training to advance.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years; coursework or project experience in criticality, radiation transport, or fuel handling preferred.

skills.name: Criticality calculations
skills.description: You run Monte Carlo transport codes such as MCNP or SCALE/KENO to compute the effective multiplication factor for fuel storage and handling configurations. You confirm results stay below the subcritical limit with margin.

skills.name: Nuclear criticality safety standards
skills.description: You apply ANSI/ANS-8 series standards to establish controls and limits for fissile material operations. You document the basis for each control parameter.

skills.name: Geometry and moderation control
skills.description: You evaluate the double contingency principle for geometry, moderation, and mass controls in storage racks and casks. You identify credible upset conditions.

skills.name: Burnup credit analysis
skills.description: You support burnup credit evaluations for spent fuel pools and dry casks using depletion and criticality sequences. You verify isotopic inputs and axial burnup profiles.

skills.name: Validation and bias determination
skills.description: You benchmark code models against critical experiment handbooks to establish calculational bias and uncertainty. You set the upper subcritical limit accordingly.

skills.name: Fissile operations review
skills.description: You review fuel handling and storage procedures for conformance with criticality controls. You participate in safety evaluations of proposed configuration changes.

roles.description: You evaluate the subcriticality of fuel storage, handling, and transport configurations for reactor plants and fuel facilities. You build Monte Carlo transport models, apply the double contingency principle, and establish controls under the ANSI/ANS-8 standards. The role protects against inadvertent criticality across the fuel lifecycle.

roles.title: Associate Thermal-Hydraulics Engineer
roles.degree_detail: You need a bachelor of science in mechanical or nuclear engineering with strong coursework in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer. Exposure to two-phase flow or system thermal-hydraulic codes through a project or internship helps. A master of science in nuclear or thermal sciences is a common path toward lead thermal-hydraulics work.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years; coursework in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and two-phase flow required.

skills.name: System code modeling
skills.description: You develop thermal-hydraulic nodalization for RELAP5 or TRACE to simulate transients and loss-of-coolant accidents. You verify nodalization sensitivity against established guidelines.

skills.name: Two-phase flow fundamentals
skills.description: You apply critical flow, flow regime, and heat transfer correlations to reactor coolant system transients. You check that correlation ranges match the conditions being analyzed.

skills.name: Containment response analysis
skills.description: You support containment pressure and temperature response calculations for mass and energy release events. You confirm peak values remain below design limits.

skills.name: Decay heat evaluation
skills.description: You apply ANS decay heat standards to establish the heat load driving long-term cooling analyses. You document the applicable uncertainty multiplier.

skills.name: Code output verification
skills.description: You check energy and mass conservation and compare results against separate-effects benchmarks. You document any user choices that affect results.

skills.name: Data reduction and plotting
skills.description: You post-process large transient datasets with Python to produce figures for calculation packages. You keep processing reproducible and version controlled.

roles.description: You support thermal-hydraulic safety analyses that demonstrate adequate core cooling during transients and accidents. You build system code models, apply heat transfer and two-phase flow correlations, and reduce results for calculation packages. The role develops the modeling skills needed for licensed transient and LOCA analysis on current and advanced reactors.

roles.title: Reliability Data Analyst
roles.degree_detail: You need at least an associate degree in engineering technology, data analytics, or a related technical field, or a bachelor degree for faster advancement. Database and spreadsheet skills are essential, and familiarity with plant maintenance systems is valued. Many analysts pursue a bachelor degree to move into PRA engineering roles.
roles.experience: 0 to 3 years supporting reliability, maintenance, or equipment data programs; associate degree with relevant experience accepted.

skills.name: Failure data collection
skills.description: You gather component failure and demand data from work orders, maintenance records, and the equipment reliability program. You screen records for PRA applicability and completeness.

skills.name: Failure mode coding
skills.description: You classify events by component type and failure mode consistent with industry taxonomies used in NUREG/CR-6928. You keep coding consistent so trends stay meaningful.

skills.name: Database and query work
skills.description: You maintain reliability databases and write SQL or spreadsheet queries to extract failure populations and exposure counts. You check data integrity before handing results to analysts.

skills.name: Maintenance Rule support
skills.description: You track system and component performance against Maintenance Rule (a1/a2) criteria and prepare performance summaries. You flag functional failures for engineering review.

skills.name: Data trending and reporting
skills.description: You build trend charts and reliability summaries that feed PRA data updates and management reviews. You present data clearly with sources noted.

skills.name: Records and quality control
skills.description: You maintain traceable records under the plant quality program so data updates are auditable. You verify counts and exposure times before issue.

roles.description: You collect, code, and maintain the equipment reliability data that feeds the plant PRA model and the Maintenance Rule program. You screen failure records, manage reliability databases, and produce trend summaries for engineers and management. The role is a practical entry point for data-focused staff supporting risk analysis.

roles.title: PRA Engineer
roles.degree_detail: You need a bachelor of science in nuclear, mechanical, or systems engineering; a master of science in reliability or nuclear engineering is common at this level. Deep working knowledge of CAFTA or SAPHIRE and the PRA Standard is expected. A Professional Engineer license strengthens credibility on licensing applications.
roles.experience: 4 to 8 years in probabilistic risk assessment, reliability engineering, or systems analysis.

skills.name: Model development and maintenance
skills.description: You own portions of the full-power internal events PRA model in CAFTA or SAPHIRE, including fault trees, event trees, and recovery actions. You keep the model current with plant configuration changes.

skills.name: Risk quantification
skills.description: You quantify core damage frequency and large early release frequency and interpret cutsets and importance measures. You identify the dominant risk contributors and explain them to engineering.

skills.name: Risk-informed applications
skills.description: You perform evaluations under 10 CFR 50.69, Technical Specification changes under RG 1.177, and Maintenance Rule (a)(4) configuration risk. You defend the risk acceptance basis of each application.

skills.name: Common cause and HRA integration
skills.description: You incorporate common cause failure groups and human reliability analysis results into the model. You confirm parameter sources and dependency assumptions are documented.

skills.name: PRA standard conformance
skills.description: You assess model technical adequacy against the ASME/ANS PRA Standard and resolve peer review findings and facts and observations. You track open items to closure.

skills.name: Sensitivity and uncertainty analysis
skills.description: You run parametric and state-of-knowledge uncertainty analyses to test the robustness of results. You communicate the impact of key assumptions.

roles.description: You develop, quantify, and apply the plant probabilistic risk assessment model to support risk-informed decisions. You own model elements, perform risk applications, and resolve peer review findings against the ASME/ANS PRA Standard. Your results directly inform licensing submittals, maintenance planning, and plant modifications.

roles.title: Thermal-Hydraulics Engineer
roles.degree_detail: You need a bachelor of science in mechanical or nuclear engineering, with a master of science in thermal-fluid or nuclear sciences common for lead work. Mastery of a system thermal-hydraulic code such as RELAP5 or TRACE is essential. A Professional Engineer license supports sign-off authority on safety analyses.
roles.experience: 4 to 8 years performing transient and accident thermal-hydraulic analysis.

skills.name: LOCA and transient analysis
skills.description: You perform large and small break loss-of-coolant and non-LOCA transient analyses with RELAP5, TRACE, or vendor codes. You demonstrate that acceptance criteria such as peak clad temperature are met.

skills.name: Evaluation model methodology
skills.description: You apply approved evaluation models and best-estimate plus uncertainty methods consistent with Regulatory Guide 1.157 and 10 CFR 50.46. You maintain the methodology basis documentation.

skills.name: Containment and pressure analysis
skills.description: You analyze containment and compartment pressure and temperature response to mass and energy releases. You confirm equipment qualification and structural limits are protected.

skills.name: Code validation and benchmarking
skills.description: You benchmark models against integral and separate-effects test data to justify code applicability. You quantify code and model uncertainty.

skills.name: Advanced reactor modeling
skills.description: You adapt thermal-hydraulic methods to SMR and advanced reactor designs, including passive cooling and non-water coolants. You identify where legacy correlations no longer apply.

skills.name: Analysis documentation and defense
skills.description: You prepare calculation packages and support regulatory audits and requests for additional information. You explain modeling choices to reviewers and the NRC.

roles.description: You perform the thermal-hydraulic transient and accident analyses that prove adequate core and containment cooling. You apply approved evaluation models, benchmark codes against test data, and defend results to regulators. Your work extends from the operating fleet to passive-safety SMRs and advanced reactors.

roles.title: Severe Accident Analyst
roles.degree_detail: You typically need a master of science or PhD in nuclear engineering, with specialization in severe accident phenomena, thermal-hydraulics, or source term analysis. Deep experience with MAAP or MELCOR is expected. The depth of phenomenology involved makes graduate study the normal path into this role.
roles.experience: 5 to 9 years in severe accident, source term, or Level 2 PRA analysis.

skills.name: Severe accident progression modeling
skills.description: You model core degradation, relocation, and containment challenges using MAAP or MELCOR. You evaluate hydrogen generation, containment pressurization, and failure modes.

skills.name: Source term and release analysis
skills.description: You calculate fission product release and transport to support Level 2 PRA and offsite dose. You apply the relevant source term basis such as alternative source term guidance.

skills.name: Level 2 PRA development
skills.description: You build containment event trees and release category binning that link core damage states to release outcomes. You quantify large early release frequency.

skills.name: Mitigation strategy evaluation
skills.description: You assess FLEX and severe accident management guideline actions for their effectiveness in arresting progression. You credit equipment and timing realistically.

skills.name: Code benchmarking
skills.description: You compare MAAP and MELCOR results and reconcile differences against experiments and the Fukushima and TMI data. You document the basis for code selection.

skills.name: Beyond-design-basis evaluation
skills.description: You analyze beyond-design-basis external events and extended loss of AC power scenarios. You identify cliff-edge effects and recovery timing.

roles.description: You analyze how accidents progress beyond the design basis into core damage, containment challenge, and radiological release. You run MAAP and MELCOR, build Level 2 PRA logic, and evaluate severe accident mitigation strategies. Your work supports emergency planning, source term definition, and risk-informed severe accident management.

roles.title: Fuel Safety Engineer
roles.degree_detail: You need a bachelor of science in nuclear or mechanical engineering, with a master of science common for advanced fuel modeling. Strong grounding in reactor physics, heat transfer, and materials behavior is important. Experience with fuel vendor methodologies and codes is a significant advantage.
roles.experience: 4 to 8 years in fuel performance, core design, or reload safety analysis.

skills.name: Reload safety analysis
skills.description: You perform the cycle-specific reload safety evaluation that confirms each core design stays within the safety analysis limits. You verify key parameters against the reference bounding analysis.

skills.name: Fuel performance modeling
skills.description: You run fuel rod codes to evaluate clad stress, fission gas release, and thermal-mechanical limits across burnup. You confirm compliance with licensed fuel design limits.

skills.name: Thermal limits evaluation
skills.description: You establish and verify departure from nucleate boiling and linear heat rate limits that protect fuel integrity. You tie limits to the technical specifications.

skills.name: Transient fuel behavior
skills.description: You analyze fuel response during overpower and rod ejection events, including fuel enthalpy criteria. You confirm margins to fuel failure and dispersal thresholds.

skills.name: Core design interface
skills.description: You coordinate with reactor physics to confirm peaking factors and loading patterns remain within analyzed bounds. You flag designs that erode margin.

skills.name: Licensing basis management
skills.description: You maintain the fuel safety licensing basis and support fuel vendor and regulatory interactions. You document the basis for each reload cycle.

roles.description: You demonstrate that each fuel reload and the fuel itself remain within thermal, mechanical, and transient safety limits. You perform reload safety evaluations, run fuel performance codes, and establish thermal limits that protect fuel integrity. Your work directly governs how each core is designed and operated.

roles.title: Human Reliability Analyst
roles.degree_detail: You need a bachelor of science in nuclear or industrial engineering, human factors, cognitive psychology, or a related field. Knowledge of plant operations and emergency procedures is essential, and a master of science in human factors or reliability is common. Former operations or simulator experience strengthens credibility.
roles.experience: 4 to 8 years in human reliability analysis, human factors, or PRA.

skills.name: HRA method application
skills.description: You quantify human error probabilities using methods such as THERP, SPAR-H, and the EPRI HRA Calculator. You select the method that fits the action and available data.

skills.name: Operator action modeling
skills.description: You define pre-initiator and post-initiator human failure events and integrate them into the PRA model. You confirm timing and procedural context for each action.

skills.name: Performance shaping factors
skills.description: You evaluate stress, complexity, available time, and cues that drive error likelihood. You document the basis for each performance shaping factor assignment.

skills.name: Procedure and simulator review
skills.description: You review emergency operating procedures and observe simulator scenarios to validate feasibility and timing. You adjust assumptions to match operating crew behavior.

skills.name: Dependency analysis
skills.description: You assess dependencies between multiple operator actions in the same sequence. You apply dependency rules so combined probabilities stay realistic.

skills.name: Standard conformance for HRA
skills.description: You meet the human reliability supporting requirements of the ASME/ANS PRA Standard. You resolve peer review findings on HRA technical adequacy.

roles.description: You quantify the likelihood that operators succeed or fail at the actions credited in the plant risk model. You apply established HRA methods, model operator actions, and validate feasibility through procedure and simulator review. Your estimates are often among the most influential contributors to the overall risk result.

roles.title: Principal PRA Engineer
roles.degree_detail: You typically hold a master of science or PhD in nuclear engineering or reliability engineering. Many years of hands-on PRA across multiple hazard groups and leadership in industry peer reviews define this level. A Professional Engineer license and recognized standing in PRA technical bodies are common.
roles.experience: 12 or more years in PRA with recognized technical leadership and peer review participation.

skills.name: PRA methodology ownership
skills.description: You set the technical approach for the plant or fleet PRA, including internal events, fire, flood, and external hazards models. You decide how new methods and standards are adopted.

skills.name: Risk-informed licensing strategy
skills.description: You lead complex applications such as 10 CFR 50.69, risk-informed Technical Specifications, and NFPA 805 fire protection. You shape the risk acceptance argument presented to the NRC.

skills.name: Peer review leadership
skills.description: You lead and participate in industry PRA peer reviews against the ASME/ANS PRA Standard. You judge technical adequacy and disposition facts and observations across capability categories.

skills.name: Multi-hazard integration
skills.description: You integrate seismic, fire, and flooding PRA results with internal events into a coherent risk profile. You reconcile overlapping assumptions across models.

skills.name: Advanced reactor PRA
skills.description: You develop risk frameworks for SMRs and advanced reactors, including the technology-inclusive and risk-informed approaches in licensing modernization. You adapt methods where operating experience is limited.

skills.name: Regulatory interface
skills.description: You represent the organization in high-stakes technical interactions with the NRC and industry groups. You defend methods and results under scrutiny.

roles.description: You are the senior technical authority for probabilistic risk assessment across a plant or fleet. You own PRA methodology, lead the most consequential risk-informed licensing efforts, and drive peer reviews against the ASME/ANS PRA Standard. You set the direction for applying PRA to SMRs and advanced reactor licensing.

roles.title: Safety Analysis Manager
roles.degree_detail: You need a bachelor of science in nuclear or mechanical engineering, and a master of science is common. Extensive hands-on safety analysis experience plus demonstrated leadership are required. A Professional Engineer license is typically expected for approval authority on safety analyses.
roles.experience: 12 or more years in safety analysis with several years leading engineering teams.

skills.name: Analysis program leadership
skills.description: You lead the team responsible for design-basis accident, transient, and containment analyses for the plant or fleet. You balance technical quality, schedule, and regulatory commitments.

skills.name: Licensing basis oversight
skills.description: You maintain the integrity of the safety analysis report and the plant licensing basis. You approve 10 CFR 50.59 evaluations and safety analysis changes.

skills.name: Technical review and approval
skills.description: You provide independent review and final approval of safety-related calculations and methodologies. You hold analysts to the applicable NUREG and regulatory guides.

skills.name: Regulatory commitment management
skills.description: You oversee responses to NRC requests for additional information and inspection findings. You ensure commitments are tracked and met.

skills.name: Resource and competency planning
skills.description: You staff and develop a team with the right mix of thermal-hydraulics, physics, and accident analysis skills. You plan for succession on critical methodologies.

skills.name: Cross-discipline coordination
skills.description: You align safety analysis with PRA, fuel, and design engineering so inputs and assumptions stay consistent. You resolve conflicts between disciplines.

roles.description: You lead the safety analysis organization that proves the plant meets its design-basis requirements. You own the technical quality of accident and transient analyses, approve licensing basis changes, and manage regulatory interactions. You develop the engineering team and align its work with PRA, fuel, and design disciplines.

roles.title: Lead Reactor Safety Engineer
roles.degree_detail: You typically hold a master of science or PhD in nuclear engineering with breadth across reactor physics and thermal-hydraulics. A long record of licensed safety analysis and methodology development is expected. A Professional Engineer license and deep familiarity with NRC review practice are common.
roles.experience: 10 or more years spanning reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, and accident analysis.

skills.name: Integrated safety case
skills.description: You assemble the technical safety case that ties neutronics, thermal-hydraulics, fuel, and accident analysis into a coherent demonstration. You confirm assumptions are consistent across disciplines.

skills.name: Deterministic and risk-informed balance
skills.description: You apply both deterministic defense-in-depth and risk-informed insights to safety decisions. You weigh PRA results against design-basis margins.

skills.name: Advanced reactor safety analysis
skills.description: You lead safety evaluations for SMRs and non-light-water reactors, including passive systems and novel coolants. You identify where established codes and criteria require new validation.

skills.name: Methodology qualification
skills.description: You qualify and document analytical methods and codes for licensing use. You defend code applicability and uncertainty treatment to regulators.

skills.name: Technical mentorship
skills.description: You mentor analysts across physics and thermal-hydraulics and review their most difficult calculations. You raise the technical bar of the group.

skills.name: Safety evaluation of changes
skills.description: You lead safety evaluations of design modifications and new fuel or operating strategies. You determine the analyses required to support each change.

roles.description: You are the senior engineering lead responsible for the integrated reactor safety case across physics, thermal-hydraulics, and accident analysis. You balance deterministic defense-in-depth with risk-informed insights and qualify the methods used for licensing. You lead safety analysis for advanced reactor designs where new validation is required.

roles.title: Risk Management Director
roles.degree_detail: You typically hold a master of science or PhD in nuclear engineering, often with additional business or management education. A long career spanning PRA, safety analysis, and regulatory leadership is required. A Professional Engineer license and senior standing in industry risk organizations are common.
roles.experience: 15 or more years in nuclear safety and risk with senior leadership responsibility.

skills.name: Risk governance
skills.description: You set the enterprise framework for how nuclear risk is assessed, communicated, and acted on. You define risk acceptance criteria and escalation thresholds.

skills.name: Risk-informed decision strategy
skills.description: You direct how PRA insights drive investment, maintenance, and licensing decisions across the fleet. You align risk management with operational and business priorities.

skills.name: Regulatory and industry engagement
skills.description: You represent the organization with the NRC, INPO, and industry owners groups on risk policy. You influence the direction of risk-informed regulation.

skills.name: PRA program oversight
skills.description: You ensure PRA models, standards conformance, and peer reviews meet quality and currency expectations fleet-wide. You hold programs accountable for technical adequacy.

skills.name: Organizational safety culture
skills.description: You champion a questioning attitude and conservative decision-making in the face of uncertainty. You ensure risk insights are not overridden without justification.

skills.name: Portfolio and talent leadership
skills.description: You build and resource the risk and safety analysis organization and its leadership pipeline. You prioritize across competing analytical demands.

roles.description: You hold executive accountability for nuclear risk management across a plant or fleet. You set risk governance and acceptance criteria, direct how PRA insights shape fleet decisions, and represent the organization to regulators and industry bodies. You lead the risk and safety analysis organization and sustain a strong safety culture.

roles.title: Principal Severe Accident and Source Term Analyst
roles.degree_detail: You typically hold a PhD or master of science in nuclear engineering with deep specialization in severe accident phenomenology and radiological source term. Extensive experience with MAAP and MELCOR and with Level 2 PRA is required. Recognized standing in severe accident research and industry working groups is common at this level.
roles.experience: 12 or more years in severe accident phenomenology, source term, and Level 2 PRA.

skills.name: Severe accident code authority
skills.description: You are the lead authority on MAAP and MELCOR application, including model selection and uncertainty treatment. You arbitrate differences between codes for licensing use.

skills.name: Source term methodology
skills.description: You define the source term basis for design-basis and beyond-design-basis events, including alternative source term applications. You defend the methodology to the NRC.

skills.name: Level 2 PRA leadership
skills.description: You own the containment performance and release frequency model and its integration with Level 1 PRA. You direct containment event tree and release category development.

skills.name: External hazard and multi-unit risk
skills.description: You lead severe accident evaluation of external events and multi-unit site risk informed by the Fukushima lessons. You capture cross-unit dependencies and shared resources.

skills.name: Mitigation and SAMG strategy
skills.description: You evaluate and shape severe accident management guidelines and FLEX strategies at a program level. You confirm strategies are effective across the dominant sequences.

skills.name: Research and validation direction
skills.description: You guide benchmarking against experiments and international research programs. You determine where phenomenological uncertainty must be reduced.

roles.description: You are the senior technical authority on severe accident progression, source term, and Level 2 PRA. You lead MAAP and MELCOR application, define the source term basis for licensing, and own the containment release model. Your work shapes emergency planning, severe accident management strategy, and beyond-design-basis risk understanding.

roles.title: Nuclear Security Officer
roles.degree_detail: A high school diploma or GED is the typical minimum, and many officers enter directly from military service, corrections, or civilian law enforcement where they gained firearms and tactical experience. New hires complete the site-specific nuclear security officer training and qualification program under 10 CFR 73 Appendix B before standing armed posts. Some utilities prefer a 2-year criminal justice degree for advancement.
roles.experience: 0 to 2 years; military, corrections, or law enforcement background strongly preferred

skills.name: Armed Response & Firearms Proficiency
skills.description: You carry and qualify with duty firearms under the plant protective strategy and stand ready to engage an adversary force attempting sabotage or theft of special nuclear material. You requalify on the range and in tactical scenarios on the schedule set by your security training program.

skills.name: Access Control & Search
skills.description: You screen personnel, vehicles, and packages at protected and vital area portals using metal detectors, explosive trace detection, and hand searches. You enforce the site access authorization list and deny entry to anyone lacking unescorted access.

skills.name: Post & Patrol Operations
skills.description: You stand fixed posts and conduct roving patrols of the protected area, isolation zones, and vital equipment, logging observations and reporting degraded barriers or intrusions. You maintain situational awareness of blind spots and tampering indicators.

skills.name: Use-of-Force Decision Making
skills.description: You apply the graduated use-of-force continuum and deadly-force policy correctly under stress, consistent with 10 CFR 73 and site procedures. You can articulate the justification for any force applied.

skills.name: Contingency Response
skills.description: You execute your assigned role in security contingency plans for intrusions, bomb threats, and fires, moving to defensive positions and supporting the response matrix. You participate in force-on-force drills that test these responses.

skills.name: Radio & Alarm Communications
skills.description: You communicate clearly on secured radio nets using plain and coded language, and you respond promptly to alarm annunciations relayed from the central alarm station. You confirm and document the resolution of each alarm.

certifications: nuclear security officer qualification (site-specific per 10 CFR 73 Appendix B)
roles.description: You protect a nuclear facility against radiological sabotage and theft of special nuclear material by standing armed posts, controlling access, and responding to security events. You are the front line of the plant protective strategy and operate under the physical security plan required by 10 CFR 73. You qualify regularly on firearms and tactics and participate in realistic force-on-force exercises.

roles.title: Alarm Station Operator
roles.degree_detail: A high school diploma or GED is the typical minimum, and most operators promote from the nuclear security officer ranks after demonstrating reliability and judgment. Training covers the site intrusion detection and access control systems plus the physical security plan. A 2-year degree in criminal justice or security technology can speed advancement into supervision.
roles.experience: 1 to 3 years in security operations or dispatch; prior nuclear security officer time is common

skills.name: Intrusion Detection System Monitoring
skills.description: You monitor perimeter intrusion detection, microwave and fence sensors, and balanced magnetic switches from the central or secondary alarm station. You assess each annunciation and dispatch response to confirm or clear it within required response times.

skills.name: CCTV Assessment
skills.description: You use fixed and pan-tilt-zoom cameras to visually assess alarms and verify the cause before classifying an event. You recognize nuisance sources such as wildlife and weather versus genuine intrusion attempts.

skills.name: Access Control System Administration
skills.description: You operate the electronic access control system to grant, deny, and log entries to protected and vital areas in real time. You maintain the integrity of the access authorization database and badge inventory.

skills.name: Alarm Response Coordination
skills.description: You direct responding officers to alarm locations and track their movements while keeping the shift supervisor informed. You coordinate compensatory measures when a sensor or barrier is degraded.

skills.name: Secure Communications & Logkeeping
skills.description: You maintain continuous radio contact with posts and patrols and keep an accurate security event log. You document every alarm, its assessment, and its resolution for the record and later review.

skills.name: Central Alarm Station Hardening Awareness
skills.description: You understand why the alarm station is bullet-resisting and continuously staffed, and you protect it against unauthorized entry. You know the procedures to transfer functions to the secondary alarm station if the primary is compromised.

certifications: nuclear security officer qualification (site-specific per 10 CFR 73 Appendix B)
roles.description: You operate the central or secondary alarm station, the hardened nerve center of plant security, monitoring intrusion detection and access control systems. You assess alarms, dispatch armed response, and coordinate compensatory measures when barriers are degraded. Your station is continuously staffed and bullet-resisting as required by 10 CFR 73.

roles.title: Access Control Specialist
roles.degree_detail: A 2-year degree in criminal justice, human resources, or a related field is typical, though strong candidates enter with a high school diploma plus screening or security experience. On-the-job training covers the access authorization and fitness-for-duty procedures. The role is a common entry point for those who later move into security management or EP planning.
roles.experience: 0 to 3 years in security, HR screening, or badging operations

skills.name: Unescorted Access Authorization Processing
skills.description: You process applications for unescorted access, verifying background investigations, psychological evaluations, and employment history against 10 CFR 73.56 requirements. You ensure no one receives a badge before every element clears.

skills.name: Fitness-for-Duty Program Support
skills.description: You support drug and alcohol testing and behavioral observation under the 10 CFR 26 fitness-for-duty program. You coordinate testing logistics and protect the confidentiality of results.

skills.name: Badging & Credential Issuance
skills.description: You issue, deactivate, and audit photo badges and access credentials tied to the access control system. You immediately revoke access when authorization is withdrawn or employment ends.

skills.name: Visitor & Escort Management
skills.description: You process visitors, verify their sponsors, and brief escorts on their responsibilities inside protected and vital areas. You track visitor counts and ensure no unescorted gaps occur.

skills.name: Records Integrity & Auditing
skills.description: You maintain accurate access authorization records that withstand NRC inspection and internal audit. You reconcile the badge population against the authorized list on the required cycle.

skills.name: Insider Mitigation Awareness
skills.description: You apply the behavioral observation and access reauthorization elements that reduce insider threat. You report aberrant behavior through the established program channels.

roles.description: You manage the unescorted access authorization program that decides who may enter a nuclear facility without an escort. You verify background investigations, coordinate fitness-for-duty testing, and issue and revoke badges in line with 10 CFR 73.56 and 10 CFR 26. Your accuracy keeps unauthorized and unreliable individuals outside the protected area.

roles.title: Emergency Preparedness Coordinator
roles.degree_detail: A 4-year degree in emergency management, nuclear or health physics, a science, or a related field is the usual entry path. Some coordinators transfer from plant operations or security after learning the facility. Employers value FEMA Emergency Management Institute independent study coursework completed early in the role.
roles.experience: 0 to 3 years; internships or plant operations exposure helpful

skills.name: Emergency Plan Familiarity
skills.description: You know the site emergency plan and implementing procedures required by 10 CFR 50.47 and 10 CFR 50 Appendix E. You can locate the right procedure for a given emergency action level and classification.

skills.name: Emergency Response Facility Readiness
skills.description: You maintain the technical support center, operations support center, and emergency operations facility in a ready state. You verify equipment, communications, and supplies so the facilities can be activated on demand.

skills.name: Drill Logistics Support
skills.description: You schedule, set up, and support emergency drills and tabletop exercises, preparing scenarios and tracking participation. You help capture controller observations for later evaluation.

skills.name: Notification System Operation
skills.description: You operate and test emergency notification systems, including sirens and the prompt notification path to state and local officials. You document test results and failures for correction.

skills.name: Emergency Response Organization Tracking
skills.description: You track the qualification and on-call status of the emergency response organization so every position is covered. You identify and escalate staffing gaps before they become findings.

skills.name: Records & Procedure Control
skills.description: You keep emergency plan documents, call lists, and agreements current and under formal document control. You route revisions for review and confirm obsolete copies are removed.

roles.description: You support the plant emergency preparedness program by keeping emergency response facilities, procedures, and the response organization ready to activate. You help run drills, maintain notification systems, and track qualifications under 10 CFR 50.47 and 10 CFR 50 Appendix E. This role builds the foundation for a career as an EP planner or manager.

roles.title: Radiological Emergency Response Technician
roles.degree_detail: A 2-year degree in radiation protection technology, nuclear technology, or applied science is common, often earned at a community or technical college with a nuclear program. Many technicians cross-train from radiation protection into the emergency response organization. Longer-term, pursuing NRRPT registration strengthens advancement into dose assessment and EP planning roles.
roles.experience: 0 to 3 years; radiation protection or HAZMAT background helpful

skills.name: Field Monitoring & Survey
skills.description: You deploy with field monitoring teams to measure dose rates and collect air, soil, and vegetation samples during a radiological emergency. You report readings accurately so dose projections reflect real conditions.

skills.name: Radiation Instrument Use
skills.description: You operate and source-check survey meters, air samplers, and dosimetry used in emergency response. You recognize when an instrument reads off-scale or has failed and switch to a backup.

skills.name: Dose Assessment Support
skills.description: You feed field data into the dose assessment process that supports protective action recommendations for the public. You understand how plume direction and release rate drive the projected dose.

skills.name: Contamination Control & Decon
skills.description: You perform contamination surveys and personnel decontamination at reception and monitoring points. You control the spread of contamination between zones.

skills.name: Protective Action Awareness
skills.description: You understand how emergency classifications translate into protective actions such as sheltering and evacuation within the plume exposure pathway EPZ. You know your role in supporting those actions.

skills.name: Emergency Communications
skills.description: You relay field readings clearly to the dose assessment staff and emergency coordinator over radio or phone. You confirm your location and the units of every measurement you report.
