certifications: NRRPT (Registered Radiation Protection Technologist) eligibility track
roles.description: You serve on field monitoring and dose assessment teams during a radiological emergency, measuring radiation in the environment and supporting protective action recommendations for the public. You operate survey instruments, control contamination, and feed real field data into the dose projection process. Your measurements help officials decide whether to shelter or evacuate residents in the emergency planning zone.

roles.title: Security Shift Officer (Response Team)
roles.degree_detail: A high school diploma or GED is the minimum, and response team members usually promote from the nuclear security officer ranks after demonstrating superior firearms and tactical skill. Military infantry, special operations, or police tactical experience is highly valued. Members complete enhanced tactical qualification and maintain it through frequent drills and force-on-force exercises.
roles.experience: 2 to 4 years as a nuclear security officer; prior military or SWAT experience valued

skills.name: Tactical Response & Fire-and-Movement
skills.description: You execute defensive positions, fire-and-movement, and interdiction tactics as part of the armed response team defending against the design basis threat. You rehearse these in force-on-force exercises against a mock adversary.

skills.name: Defensive Position Operations
skills.description: You occupy and fight from hardened bullet-resisting enclosures and prepared firing positions covering vital equipment. You understand your sectors of fire and the protective strategy timeline.

skills.name: Advanced Weapons Handling
skills.description: You maintain proficiency with rifles and other enhanced weapons authorized under the site protective strategy. You keep weapons and ammunition secured and accounted for in the armory.

skills.name: Target Set Protection
skills.description: You understand the target sets an adversary would need to reach to cause radiological sabotage and how the response strategy denies them. You prioritize defense of the most critical equipment.

skills.name: Force-on-Force Participation
skills.description: You participate in NRC-evaluated and self-assessment force-on-force exercises using laser engagement gear, treating them as realistic tests of the protective strategy. You incorporate lessons learned into your tactics.

skills.name: Less-Lethal & Barrier Tactics
skills.description: You employ delay barriers, vehicle barriers, and less-lethal options as part of a layered defense. You coordinate with the alarm station to time your response to the adversary's movement.

certifications: nuclear security officer qualification (site-specific per 10 CFR 73 Appendix B)
roles.description: You are a member of the armed response team that defends the plant against the design basis threat defined in 10 CFR 73. You train in tactics, fight from defensive positions, and protect vital target sets from an adversary force. You regularly prove the protective strategy in NRC force-on-force exercises.

roles.title: Emergency Preparedness Planner
roles.degree_detail: A 4-year degree in emergency management, nuclear engineering, health physics, or a science is standard, and some planners hold public administration degrees. Most advance from an EP coordinator role or transfer from operations after gaining plant knowledge. FEMA Emergency Management Institute coursework and the NEI EP qualification program are expected credentials.
roles.experience: 4 to 8 years in emergency preparedness, operations, or emergency management

skills.name: Emergency Plan Development
skills.description: You write and maintain the site emergency plan and implementing procedures to satisfy 10 CFR 50.47 planning standards and 10 CFR 50 Appendix E. You keep emergency action levels aligned with the NEI 99-01 methodology endorsed by the NRC.

skills.name: Emergency Action Level Scheme Maintenance
skills.description: You maintain the emergency action level scheme that classifies events into notification of unusual event, alert, site area emergency, and general emergency. You validate that initiating conditions map correctly to plant instrumentation.

skills.name: Offsite Coordination
skills.description: You coordinate with state and local emergency management, FEMA, and offsite response organizations under the FEMA REP program. You maintain letters of agreement and support offsite evacuation time estimate updates.

skills.name: 10 CFR 50.54(q) Change Evaluation
skills.description: You perform and document 10 CFR 50.54(q) evaluations to determine whether a plan change reduces effectiveness and requires prior NRC approval. You defend these screenings during inspection.

skills.name: Regulatory Interface
skills.description: You interface with NRC inspectors and respond to requests during EP baseline inspections. You track and close EP commitments and corrective actions in the corrective action program.

skills.name: Protective Action Strategy
skills.description: You develop protective action recommendations for the plume exposure and ingestion pathway emergency planning zones. You ensure recommendations account for evacuation time estimates and dose projections.

roles.description: You own the content of the plant emergency plan, keeping its procedures, emergency action levels, and offsite agreements compliant with 10 CFR 50.47 and 10 CFR 50 Appendix E. You coordinate with FEMA, the state, and local jurisdictions under the REP program and evaluate every plan change under 10 CFR 50.54(q). You are the technical expert the plant relies on during EP inspections.

roles.title: Security Supervisor
roles.degree_detail: A 2-year degree in criminal justice or security management is common, and many supervisors earn a 4-year degree while advancing. Most promote from senior security officer or response team roles, often building on prior military or law enforcement leadership. The ASIS CPP certification signals readiness for further security management responsibility.
roles.experience: 5 to 10 years in nuclear security with demonstrated leadership

skills.name: Shift Security Supervision
skills.description: You lead a shift of armed officers and alarm station operators, setting post assignments and ensuring minimum staffing per the physical security plan. You make real-time decisions during alarms and contingency events.

skills.name: Protective Strategy Execution
skills.description: You direct the response to intrusions and contingencies according to the protective strategy and 10 CFR 73 requirements. You order and track compensatory measures when equipment or barriers degrade.

skills.name: Security Training & Qualification Oversight
skills.description: You verify that every officer on your shift is current on firearms, tactics, and medical and physical fitness qualifications. You remove unqualified personnel from armed posts.

skills.name: Incident Command & Documentation
skills.description: You run the initial security response, coordinate with local law enforcement, and ensure the security event is logged and reported accurately. You preserve evidence and complete required notifications.

skills.name: Force-on-Force Leadership
skills.description: You lead your shift through force-on-force exercises and self-assessments, then drive corrective actions from the findings. You use drill performance to coach individual officers.

skills.name: Fatigue & Fitness-for-Duty Management
skills.description: You manage work-hour limits and fatigue rules under 10 CFR 26 so that armed officers remain fit for duty. You intervene when behavioral or fitness concerns arise.

certifications: nuclear security officer qualification (site-specific per 10 CFR 73 Appendix B)
roles.description: You supervise a security shift, directing armed officers and alarm station operators to execute the plant protective strategy under 10 CFR 73. You command the initial response to security events, manage compensatory measures, and keep your team qualified and fit for duty. You are accountable for shift readiness and for leading your officers through force-on-force exercises.

roles.title: Nuclear Cyber Security Analyst
roles.degree_detail: A 4-year degree in cyber security, computer science, information technology, or engineering is the standard entry. Industrial control system or operational technology experience sets strong candidates apart because nuclear cyber work is OT-centric. The GICSP certification is especially valued, with CISSP common for those moving toward program leadership.
roles.experience: 3 to 7 years in cyber security, ideally with OT or industrial control systems

skills.name: 10 CFR 73.54 Cyber Program Implementation
skills.description: You implement and maintain the cyber security program required by 10 CFR 73.54 to protect critical digital assets from attacks that could affect safety, security, and emergency preparedness functions. You apply the controls derived from NEI 08-09.

skills.name: Critical Digital Asset Analysis
skills.description: You identify and classify critical digital assets within safety, security, and EP systems and maintain the CDA inventory. You assess how each asset connects to others across security levels.

skills.name: Defensive Architecture & Isolation
skills.description: You enforce the defensive architecture that isolates the highest security levels using deterministic one-way data devices and strict boundary controls. You verify that no pathway bypasses the defensive levels.

skills.name: Security Control Assessment
skills.description: You assess technical, operational, and management security controls on critical digital assets and document deviations with alternate controls. You keep the controls effective as systems change.

skills.name: Portable Media & Mobile Device Control
skills.description: You control portable media and mobile devices, scanning them before use to prevent introducing malware into control systems. You audit media use against procedure.

skills.name: Vulnerability & Patch Evaluation
skills.description: You evaluate vulnerabilities and vendor patches for operational technology where uptime and safety constraints forbid routine patching. You test and schedule changes without disrupting plant functions.

certifications: GICSP (GIAC Global Industrial Cyber Security Professional)
roles.description: You protect the plant's critical digital assets, the computers and controls supporting safety, security, and emergency preparedness, under the 10 CFR 73.54 cyber security rule. You classify assets, enforce the defensive architecture that isolates them, and assess security controls using the NEI 08-09 framework. You bridge IT security practice and the realities of nuclear operational technology.

roles.title: Safeguards & Material Control and Accounting Specialist
roles.degree_detail: A 4-year degree in nuclear engineering, chemistry, physics, health physics, or a quantitative science is typical because the role is measurement and statistics intensive. Experience in fuel-cycle operations or radiochemistry is a strong foundation. Involvement with the Institute of Nuclear Materials Management supports professional growth toward safeguards program leadership.
roles.experience: 3 to 8 years in nuclear material accounting, health physics, or fuel-cycle operations

skills.name: Material Control & Accounting Under 10 CFR 74
skills.description: You maintain the material control and accounting program that tracks special nuclear material inventories under 10 CFR 74. You ensure book inventories reconcile with physical inventories within required limits.

skills.name: Physical Inventory & Measurement
skills.description: You plan and execute physical inventories, applying measurement and sampling methods to quantify special nuclear material accurately. You evaluate inventory differences and investigate anomalies.

skills.name: Material Balance & ID Evaluation
skills.description: You compute material balances and evaluate inventory differences against statistical alarm limits to detect possible loss or diversion. You document and resolve each significant difference.

skills.name: Item Control & Tamper Indicating Devices
skills.description: You apply item control, seals, and tamper indicating devices to containers of special nuclear material. You verify seal integrity and chain of custody during movements.

skills.name: Nuclear Material Transaction Reporting
skills.description: You prepare nuclear material transaction and inventory reports to the NRC Nuclear Materials Management and Safeguards System on the required schedule. You ensure codes and quantities are reported accurately.

skills.name: Safeguards & Diversion Path Analysis
skills.description: You analyze potential diversion paths and support the integration of MC&A with physical protection. You help ensure measures detect both insider and outsider theft attempts.

certifications: INMM membership / nuclear material management training
roles.description: You run the material control and accounting program that keeps special nuclear material fully accounted for at a fuel-cycle facility or reactor under 10 CFR 74. You conduct physical inventories, compute material balances, and report transactions to the NRC safeguards system. Your work provides timely detection of any loss or diversion of nuclear material.

roles.title: Drill & Exercise Lead
roles.degree_detail: A 4-year degree in emergency management, a science, or a related field is standard, and many leads advance from EP planner or operations training roles. The Homeland Security Exercise and Evaluation Program methodology and the FEMA Master Exercise Practitioner credential are highly relevant. Experience as a shift technical advisor or control room operator helps in building credible scenarios.
roles.experience: 5 to 9 years in emergency preparedness, operations, or training

skills.name: Scenario Design
skills.description: You design realistic drill and exercise scenarios that drive the emergency response organization through emergency classifications, notifications, and protective action decisions. You build in events that test weak areas without being transparent to players.

skills.name: Biennial Exercise Management
skills.description: You plan and run the full-participation biennial exercise evaluated by the NRC and FEMA under 10 CFR 50 Appendix E and the REP program. You coordinate offsite jurisdictions so their players exercise with the plant.

skills.name: Controller & Evaluator Coordination
skills.description: You train and direct controllers and evaluators, ensuring they inject events on schedule and capture objective performance data. You keep the exercise on its timeline without over-controlling players.

skills.name: Performance Evaluation & Critique
skills.description: You evaluate response against measurable objectives and lead the post-exercise critique that surfaces strengths and weaknesses. You translate observations into clear, actionable findings.

skills.name: Corrective Action Integration
skills.description: You enter drill and exercise weaknesses into the corrective action program and track them to closure. You verify that corrective actions actually improve the next exercise.

skills.name: Offsite Integration & REP Coordination
skills.description: You integrate state and local responders and the FEMA REP evaluation into site exercises. You ensure notification and protective action interfaces with offsite officials work under realistic timing.

roles.description: You design and run the drills and exercises that prove the plant and offsite responders can handle a radiological emergency, including the NRC and FEMA evaluated biennial exercise. You craft scenarios, direct controllers and evaluators, and drive weaknesses into the corrective action program. Your exercises keep the emergency response organization sharp and demonstrate readiness to regulators.

roles.title: Emergency Preparedness Manager
roles.degree_detail: A 4-year degree in emergency management, engineering, or a science is expected, and many managers hold a master's in emergency management or business. The path typically runs through EP planner and supervisor roles over a decade or more. The Certified Emergency Manager and FEMA Master Exercise Practitioner credentials are strong differentiators at this level.
roles.experience: 10 or more years in emergency preparedness with supervisory experience

skills.name: EP Program Ownership
skills.description: You own the site emergency preparedness program and its compliance with 10 CFR 50.47, 10 CFR 50 Appendix E, and NRC inspection expectations. You are accountable for program health metrics and NRC performance indicators.

skills.name: Regulatory & NRC Relationship Management
skills.description: You lead the plant's interface with NRC and FEMA on emergency preparedness, including inspections, enforcement, and regulatory change. You manage license amendment and exemption requests touching the emergency plan.

skills.name: Emergency Response Organization Management
skills.description: You ensure the emergency response organization is staffed, trained, and qualified across all shifts and facilities. You oversee the duty roster and on-call augmentation that meets Appendix E response timelines.

skills.name: Budget & Resource Planning
skills.description: You plan and defend the EP budget covering facilities, notification systems, drills, and staffing. You prioritize investments that most improve emergency response capability.

skills.name: Cross-Functional Crisis Leadership
skills.description: You lead EP integration with operations, radiation protection, security, and corporate communications during actual events. You can fill the emergency director or recovery manager role in a declared emergency.

skills.name: Offsite Governmental Coordination
skills.description: You maintain relationships and agreements with state, local, and tribal authorities and FEMA under the REP program. You represent the plant in offsite planning committees and public information coordination.

roles.description: You lead the entire emergency preparedness program for a nuclear plant, accountable for compliance with 10 CFR 50.47 and 10 CFR 50 Appendix E and for the readiness of the emergency response organization. You manage the EP staff and budget, own the NRC and FEMA relationship, and can serve as emergency director during a real event. Your program protects the public living within the emergency planning zones.

roles.title: Nuclear Security Director
roles.degree_detail: A graduate degree in security management, criminal justice, homeland security, or business is common at this level, though an exceptional operational record can substitute. Many directors come from senior military, federal law enforcement, or intelligence backgrounds layered with years of nuclear security management. ASIS CPP and PSP certifications are typical, alongside executive leadership development.
roles.experience: 12 or more years in nuclear or high-consequence security, including management

skills.name: Physical Security Program Leadership
skills.description: You own the site physical security program and its compliance with 10 CFR 73, including the physical security plan, training and qualification plan, and safeguards contingency plan. You are accountable for security performance to the NRC and corporate leadership.

skills.name: Protective Strategy & Design Basis Threat
skills.description: You ensure the protective strategy defeats the design basis threat and adapts to NRC threat advisories and 10 CFR 73.55 requirements. You direct analysis of target sets and adversary pathways.

skills.name: Force-on-Force Program Accountability
skills.description: You are accountable for the force-on-force program and the plant's performance in NRC-evaluated exercises. You drive corrective actions and strategy enhancements from exercise results.

skills.name: Security Force Management
skills.description: You lead a large armed security force through supervisors and managers, overseeing staffing, training, firearms, and fitness-for-duty under 10 CFR 26. You manage labor relations and workforce retention in a demanding environment.

skills.name: Security Budget & Capital Planning
skills.description: You plan multi-million dollar security budgets and capital projects for barriers, detection, and weapons systems. You justify investments that reduce risk and maintain the protective strategy.

skills.name: Threat & Intelligence Liaison
skills.description: You coordinate with the FBI, DHS, state fusion centers, and local law enforcement on threats and integrated response. You translate intelligence into protective posture changes.

roles.description: You direct the complete physical security program for a nuclear facility, accountable for defending against the design basis threat under 10 CFR 73. You lead a large armed force, own the protective strategy and force-on-force performance, and manage the security budget and capital projects. You are the plant's senior liaison to the FBI, DHS, and law enforcement on nuclear security threats.

roles.title: Physical Security Design Lead
roles.degree_detail: A 4-year degree in electrical, mechanical, civil, or security systems engineering is standard, and many design leads hold a Professional Engineer license. Experience across security systems integration, vulnerability modeling, and nuclear engineering change processes is essential. The ASIS Physical Security Professional credential complements the engineering background.
roles.experience: 10 or more years in security systems engineering or physical protection design

skills.name: Physical Protection System Design
skills.description: You design integrated physical protection systems combining detection, delay, and response to defeat the design basis threat under 10 CFR 73.55. You balance detection probability and delay time against the response force timeline.

skills.name: Barrier & Delay Engineering
skills.description: You engineer vehicle barriers, intrusion-resistant barriers, and bullet-resisting enclosures sized to the adversary and vehicle bomb threats. You validate standoff distances and penetration delay times.

skills.name: Detection & Assessment System Design
skills.description: You specify intrusion detection sensors, CCTV assessment, and access control systems to achieve required detection and assessment performance. You design for high probability of detection with low nuisance alarm rates.

skills.name: Vulnerability Assessment & Modeling
skills.description: You lead vulnerability assessments and use path analysis and timeline modeling to find and close weaknesses in the protective system. You quantify system effectiveness against adversary scenarios.

skills.name: Design Change & Configuration Control
skills.description: You lead security system design changes through the plant's engineering change and 10 CFR 50.59-equivalent security review processes. You ensure modifications do not reduce the effectiveness of the security plan.

skills.name: Blast & Target Set Protection
skills.description: You design protection for vital target sets against sabotage, including blast effects and the land vehicle bomb design basis. You coordinate with safety engineering to protect credited equipment.

roles.description: You lead the engineering design of physical protection systems that detect, delay, and defeat adversaries attempting radiological sabotage or theft of special nuclear material under 10 CFR 73.55. You engineer barriers, detection and assessment systems, and conduct the vulnerability assessments that prove the system works. Your designs give the armed response force the time and information they need to win.

roles.title: Safeguards Program Manager
roles.degree_detail: A graduate degree in nuclear engineering, chemistry, physics, or a related quantitative field is common because the role demands deep measurement and statistical expertise. The path runs through MC&A specialist and fuel-cycle operations roles over many years. Leadership within the Institute of Nuclear Materials Management reflects the professional standing expected at this level.
roles.experience: 10 or more years in nuclear material safeguards, MC&A, or fuel-cycle operations

skills.name: Safeguards & MC&A Program Ownership
skills.description: You own the safeguards and material control and accounting program at a fuel-cycle or major nuclear facility under 10 CFR 74. You are accountable for the fundamental nuclear material controls and their regulatory compliance.

skills.name: Material Accounting System Oversight
skills.description: You oversee the nuclear material accounting systems, inventory programs, and statistical evaluation of inventory differences. You ensure the program provides timely detection of loss or diversion at required thresholds.

skills.name: IAEA & International Safeguards Interface
skills.description: You coordinate with the NRC and the IAEA on international safeguards, inspections, and additional protocol reporting where applicable. You manage facility attachments and inspector access.

skills.name: MC&A and Physical Protection Integration
skills.description: You integrate material accounting with physical protection and insider mitigation into a defense against theft and diversion. You lead diversion path analysis that spans both programs.

skills.name: Regulatory Reporting & Performance
skills.description: You ensure accurate and timely reporting to the Nuclear Materials Management and Safeguards System and manage safeguards performance metrics. You lead responses to NRC safeguards inspections.

skills.name: Program Audit & Corrective Action
skills.description: You lead internal assessments of the MC&A program and drive corrective actions for inventory and measurement weaknesses. You maintain measurement control and quality programs that keep accounting defensible.

roles.description: You manage the safeguards and material control and accounting program that keeps all special nuclear material accounted for and protected against theft and diversion under 10 CFR 74. You oversee the accounting systems, lead diversion path analysis, and interface with the NRC and where applicable the IAEA. Your program integrates material accounting with physical protection to deter and detect both insider and outsider threats.

roles.title: Nuclear Cyber Security Program Owner
roles.degree_detail: A graduate degree in cyber security, computer science, or engineering is common, though a strong operational record can substitute. The path typically runs through cyber analyst and OT security roles with years of hands-on nuclear digital asset work. CISSP and GICSP certifications are standard, paired with leadership and regulatory experience.
roles.experience: 10 or more years in cyber security with substantial operational technology and nuclear experience

skills.name: 10 CFR 73.54 Program Accountability
skills.description: You own the cyber security program required by 10 CFR 73.54 and are accountable for protecting critical digital assets supporting safety, security, and emergency preparedness functions. You defend the program's effectiveness to the NRC and executive leadership.

skills.name: NEI 08-09 Framework Governance
skills.description: You govern the security controls and defensive architecture derived from the NEI 08-09 framework across the site. You approve alternate controls and ensure the program adapts as digital systems evolve.

skills.name: Cyber Incident Response & Reporting
skills.description: You lead the cyber incident response program and ensure timely reporting of events under 10 CFR 73.77. You direct containment and recovery so that plant safety and security functions are preserved.

skills.name: OT Security Strategy & Supply Chain
skills.description: You set strategy for operational technology security, including digital asset life cycle and supply chain protections against counterfeit or tampered components. You evaluate emerging threats to industrial control systems.

skills.name: Program Integration & Governance
skills.description: You integrate cyber security with physical security, EP, and engineering change processes so digital protections are not undermined by modifications. You chair the governance that reviews changes to critical digital assets.

skills.name: Audit, Training & Culture
skills.description: You oversee program self-assessments, NRC inspection readiness, and the cyber security training that builds a strong security culture. You drive corrective actions from assessment findings to closure.

certifications: GICSP (GIAC Global Industrial Cyber Security Professional)
roles.description: You own the nuclear cyber security program, accountable for protecting the critical digital assets that support safety, security, and emergency preparedness under 10 CFR 73.54. You govern the NEI 08-09 control framework, lead cyber incident response and 10 CFR 73.77 reporting, and set the strategy for operational technology and supply chain protection. You are the plant's senior authority bridging cyber security and nuclear operations.
